Richemont has signed an agreement to sell Baume & Mercier to Italy’s Damiani Group, marking a major move in the luxury watch sector. The acquisition will expand Damiani’s hard luxury portfolio, which includes Damiani, Salvini, Bliss, Calderoni, and Murano glassmaker Venini, as well as watch and jewelry retailer Rocca. The 200-year-old Baume & Mercier will join a family-run group with a strong multi-brand distribution footprint and plans for select mono-brand boutiques. Richemont will provide operational support during a 12-month transition period. Closing is expected in summer 2026, pending customary conditions. Applied Real Intelligence (A.R.I.), a U.S.-based growth investment firm, has made a strategic investment in October’s Very Own (OVO), the lifestyle brand founded by Aubrey “Drake” Graham, Oliver El-Khatib, and Noah “40” Shebib. The deal supports OVO’s continued global expansion across e-commerce, retail, and partnerships. Founded in Toronto in 2008, OVO has grown from a music collective into a globally recognized lifestyle brand, with stores in North America and London. Under CEO Derek “Drex” Jancar, the company is scaling its operations while staying rooted in cultural credibility and creative leadership. “OVO isn’t a moment; it’s a long-term movement,” said Dr. Zack Ellison, Founder and Managing General Partner at A.R.I. “We’re proud to back a brand that blends authenticity, celebrity influence, and disciplined execution, hallmarks of the next generation of iconic consumer brands.” Nike has quietly sold RTFKT, its digital products subsidiary known for virtual sneakers and NFT collectibles, marking the end of a chapter that began with its acquisition in 2021. The sale follows Nike’s move to shutter RTFKT last year and aligns with CEO Elliott Hill’s renewed focus on core sports categories and wholesale partnerships. RTFKT (pronounced “Artifact”) was acquired under former CEO John Donahoe as part of Nike’s push into digital and direct-to-consumer channels. The buyer and deal terms were not disclosed. In a brief statement, Nike said the sale “launches a new chapter for the company and its community,” adding that it will continue investing in digital innovation, particularly through gaming partnerships and virtual wearables. Marubeni Corporation has acquired UK-based Jacobson Group, owner of heritage sneaker brand Gola, as part of its strategy to build a scalable lifestyle brand platform anchored by R.G. Barry Corporation (RGB). The acquisition marks RGB’s first roll-up deal since Marubeni acquired it in 2024. Jacobson’s portfolio, led by Gola, a British brand founded in 1905 with strong roots in sport and fashion, is distributed in over 30 countries. The deal will combine Jacobson’s brand equity with RGB’s U.S.-based sales infrastructure to drive global growth. Marubeni’s Consumer Platform U.S. is focused on building next-generation consumer businesses under the company’s GC2027 strategy. The group plans to continue expanding its brand portfolio through synergistic acquisitions that reflect evolving consumer preferences. Italian luxury apparel company Zanieri has completed its reverse merger with Everlert, Inc. (OTC: EVLI), gaining control of the public entity and integrating its operations under the Everlert corporate structure. The deal marks Everlert’s formal transition into a global luxury platform with Zanieri as its core operating business. Based in Umbria, Zanieri is a vertically integrated producer of premium cashmere, known for its end-to-end manufacturing, sustainability standards, and proprietary remote tailoring technology. Temasek will join as a minority investor, alongside existing backer Permira, which will retain a strategic minority position. The deal supports Golden Goose’s international growth while preserving its Italian craftsmanship roots. CEO Silvio Campara will continue to lead the company, with Marco Bizzarri (ex-Gucci CEO) becoming Non-Executive Chairman. The brand, known for blending luxury, lifestyle, and sportswear, has seen revenue grow from €266M in 2020 to €655M in 2024, driven by strong DTC momentum and global expansion. The transaction is expected to close in summer 2026. MadaLuxe Group has acquired a majority stake in IPPOLITA, the New York-based fine jewelry house known for its sculptural designs, artisanal craftsmanship, and global following. The deal adds to MadaLuxe’s expanding portfolio of luxury fashion and lifestyle brands across categories including apparel, accessories, home, and spirits. The acquisition aligns with MadaLuxe’s strategy to invest in heritage-driven brands with enduring cultural relevance. IPPOLITA founder Ippolita Rostagno will continue as Chief Creative Officer, leading design across the brand’s signature 18k gold and sterling silver collections. “Joining MadaLuxe opens an exciting new chapter that protects our heritage while embracing new growth,” said Rostagno. The brand, which debuted at Bergdorf Goodman, has become a defining name in accessible fine jewelry and is sold through top luxury retailers worldwide. Newly launched luxury group Hulcan, founded by MILE co-founders Joe Wilkinson and Mario Maher, has acquired iconic fashion retailer MATCHES and its in-house label RAEY. The deal marks a major move in redefining the future of luxury commerce, with the two brands set to relaunch in 2026 under Hulcan’s innovative, omnichannel model. The acquisition includes the full IP portfolio of MATCHES, positioning Hulcan to revive and evolve the storied retailer with a sharper focus on profitability, digital transformation, and cultural relevance. Backed by investors including Frasers Group, Francesco Ragazzi, PagsGroup, LVMH Luxury Ventures Advisors, and the Hermès Family, Hulcan aims to integrate commerce, culture, media, and fashion in a single ecosystem. “We’re committed to preserving MATCHES’ legacy while transforming it for a new era of luxury,” said Maher. “This acquisition is foundational to building a connected, modern group that serves both brands and the next generation of luxury consumers.” Global asset advisory firm Gordon Brothers has acquired a majority interest in the intellectual property of the Rachel Zoe brand, aiming to accelerate its growth through expanded licensing, new product categories, and broader distribution. She continues to lead the brand as Founder, Chief Creative Officer, and board member. “Rachel is a global fashion authority with a brand that resonates across style, media, and lifestyle,” said Tobias Nanda, Head of Brands at Gordon Brothers. “We’re excited to grow her legacy through strategic licensing and innovation.” Republic Brands Group (RBG) has acquired heritage fashion labels Joie, Equipment, and Current/Elliott for $36 million, forming a new division dubbed The Lux Group. The move marks a strategic expansion for RBG as it builds a portfolio of culturally resonant, commercially proven brands. Skims, the shapewear and apparel brand co-founded by Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede, has raised $225 million in a new funding round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, with participation from BDT & MSD Partners. The raise values the brand at $5 billion as it accelerates plans for product expansion, international growth, and a deeper push into physical retail. Global investment firm Carlyle has officially taken control of The Very Group, marking the end of the Barclay family’s more than 20-year ownership of the UK-based online retail giant. Abu Dhabi-based IMI, another major lender, remains a key stakeholder in the business. Homecourt, the luxury home care brand founded by Courteney Cox in 2022, has raised $8 million in Series A funding to scale its team, expand retail partnerships, and prepare for international growth. The round was led by Cult Capital with $5 million, alongside participation from existing investors and friends contributing the remaining $3 million. Known for its elevated home essentials, ranging from dish soap and surface sprays to candles and body care, Homecourt has reportedly reached $30 million in sales, with hand wash now leading in dollar volume. “Homecourt just means everything to me,” Cox said. “I needed partners who understood my obsession with detail and Cult Capital really got it.” With the investment, the brand plans to deepen its retail presence beyond Nordstrom and Bluemercury, grow its small but efficient team, and continue innovating around its best-selling CeCe fragrance line. International expansion is on the horizon, with London eyed as a potential launch point. “This brand works because I won’t settle for 99 percent,” Cox said. “It has to be perfect.” French e-commerce player Showroomprivé is divesting its 51% stake in fashion platform The Bradery, selling it back to founders Timothée Linyer and Edouard Caraco for €43.6 million. The move comes as part of a broader effort to streamline operations and strengthen the company’s financial position following a difficult fiscal year marked by a €39.7 million loss. Originally acquired in 2022 for €10.2 million, The Bradery has seen rapid growth, tripling its turnover from €21.7 million in 2021 to €62.9 million in 2024. Showroomprivé will receive an initial €17 million payment, with additional proceeds tied to performance-based milestones. The transaction is expected to close by year-end, pending regulatory approvals. Chalhoub Group has made a strategic minority investment in the menswear brand Willy Chavarria, joining existing investor FAE Fashion Ventures. The deal, reportedly under $5M, supports the label’s continued global expansion and infrastructure development. Chavarria, known for his culturally conscious, identity-driven collections, will benefit from Chalhoub’s deep operational expertise and regional retail presence across the Middle East. Founder and CEO Laure Hériard Dubreuil will retain a minority stake and continue to lead operations. Calling the deal “the start of a new chapter,” Dubreuil praised the alignment between The Webster’s vision and Frasers Group’s ambition, especially around digital innovation and brand building. Colorado-based outdoor brand Halfdays has raised $10 million in a Series A round led by Kellwood Company, with participation from Dick’s Sporting Goods Ventures, model Taylor Hill, and others. Known for redefining women’s skiwear with a stylish, functional edge, Halfdays was co-founded by Ariana Ferwerda, Karelle Golda, and Olympian Kiley McKinnon. The brand, which has gained traction over the past five years, is now shifting from survival mode to growth mode. “It’s the difference between surviving and scaling,” said Ferwerda, reflecting on the milestone moment. Fueled by strong seasonal performance and high sell-through rates, the funding will support expansion of Halfdays’ winter and ski lines, entry into year-round performance wear, accelerated wholesale partnerships with retailers like Revolve and Shopbop, and investments in brick-and-mortar retail. Closed’s headquarters will remain in Hamburg, ensuring continuity for its operations and team.
