As a private company, Guess? will have more flexibility and access to resources to support growth. Richemont has signed an agreement to sell Baume & Mercier to Italy’s Damiani Group, marking a major move in the luxury watch sector. The acquisition will expand Damiani’s hard luxury portfolio, which includes Damiani, Salvini, Bliss, Calderoni, and Murano glassmaker Venini, as well as watch and jewelry retailer Rocca. The 200-year-old Baume & Mercier will join a family-run group with a strong multi-brand distribution footprint and plans for select mono-brand boutiques. Richemont will provide operational support during a 12-month transition period. Closing is expected in summer 2026, pending customary conditions. Applied Real Intelligence (A.R.I.), a U.S.-based growth investment firm, has made a strategic investment in October’s Very Own (OVO), the lifestyle brand founded by Aubrey “Drake” Graham, Oliver El-Khatib, and Noah “40” Shebib. The deal supports OVO’s continued global expansion across e-commerce, retail, and partnerships. Founded in Toronto in 2008, OVO has grown from a music collective into a globally recognized lifestyle brand, with stores in North America and London. Under CEO Derek “Drex” Jancar, the company is scaling its operations while staying rooted in cultural credibility and creative leadership. “OVO isn’t a moment; it’s a long-term movement,” said Dr. Zack Ellison, Founder and Managing General Partner at A.R.I. “We’re proud to back a brand that blends authenticity, celebrity influence, and disciplined execution, hallmarks of the next generation of iconic consumer brands.” Nike has quietly sold RTFKT, its digital products subsidiary known for virtual sneakers and NFT collectibles, marking the end of a chapter that began with its acquisition in 2021. The sale follows Nike’s move to shutter RTFKT last year and aligns with CEO Elliott Hill’s renewed focus on core sports categories and wholesale partnerships. RTFKT (pronounced “Artifact”) was acquired under former CEO John Donahoe as part of Nike’s push into digital and direct-to-consumer channels. The buyer and deal terms were not disclosed. In a brief statement, Nike said the sale “launches a new chapter for the company and its community,” adding that it will continue investing in digital innovation, particularly through gaming partnerships and virtual wearables. Marubeni Corporation has acquired UK-based Jacobson Group, owner of heritage sneaker brand Gola, as part of its strategy to build a scalable lifestyle brand platform anchored by R.G. Barry Corporation (RGB). The acquisition marks RGB’s first roll-up deal since Marubeni acquired it in 2024. Jacobson’s portfolio, led by Gola, a British brand founded in 1905 with strong roots in sport and fashion, is distributed in over 30 countries. The deal will combine Jacobson’s brand equity with RGB’s U.S.-based sales infrastructure to drive global growth. Marubeni’s Consumer Platform U.S. is focused on building next-generation consumer businesses under the company’s GC2027 strategy. The group plans to continue expanding its brand portfolio through synergistic acquisitions that reflect evolving consumer preferences. Italian luxury apparel company Zanieri has completed its reverse merger with Everlert, Inc. (OTC: EVLI), gaining control of the public entity and integrating its operations under the Everlert corporate structure. The deal marks Everlert’s formal transition into a global luxury platform with Zanieri as its core operating business. Based in Umbria, Zanieri is a vertically integrated producer of premium cashmere, known for its end-to-end manufacturing, sustainability standards, and proprietary remote tailoring technology. The merger establishes Zanieri as the controlling shareholder, positioning the newly structured public company for global expansion and long-term growth. “This merger completes Everlert’s transition into a public company with a real operating business, meaningful scale, and international reach,” said Richard Hawkins, CEO of Everlert. “Zanieri is not simply a fashion brand, it’s an industrial luxury platform with deep manufacturing expertise and a clear strategy for disciplined global growth.” Golden Goose has announced a new investment partnership with global private equity firm HSG, which will acquire a majority stake in the next-gen luxury brand. Temasek will join as a minority investor, alongside existing backer Permira, which will retain a strategic minority position. The deal supports Golden Goose’s international growth while preserving its Italian craftsmanship roots. CEO Silvio Campara will continue to lead the company, with Marco Bizzarri (ex-Gucci CEO) becoming Non-Executive Chairman. The brand, known for blending luxury, lifestyle, and sportswear, has seen revenue grow from €266M in 2020 to €655M in 2024, driven by strong DTC momentum and global expansion. The transaction is expected to close in summer 2026. MadaLuxe Group has acquired a majority stake in IPPOLITA, the New York-based fine jewelry house known for its sculptural designs, artisanal craftsmanship, and global following. The deal adds to MadaLuxe’s expanding portfolio of luxury fashion and lifestyle brands across categories including apparel, accessories, home, and spirits. The acquisition aligns with MadaLuxe’s strategy to invest in heritage-driven brands with enduring cultural relevance. IPPOLITA founder Ippolita Rostagno will continue as Chief Creative Officer, leading design across the brand’s signature 18k gold and sterling silver collections. “Joining MadaLuxe opens an exciting new chapter that protects our heritage while embracing new growth,” said Rostagno. The brand, which debuted at Bergdorf Goodman, has become a defining name in accessible fine jewelry and is sold through top luxury retailers worldwide. Newly launched luxury group Hulcan, founded by MILE co-founders Joe Wilkinson and Mario Maher, has acquired iconic fashion retailer MATCHES and its in-house label RAEY. The deal marks a major move in redefining the future of luxury commerce, with the two brands set to relaunch in 2026 under Hulcan’s innovative, omnichannel model. The acquisition includes the full IP portfolio of MATCHES, positioning Hulcan to revive and evolve the storied retailer with a sharper focus on profitability, digital transformation, and cultural relevance. Backed by investors including Frasers Group, Francesco Ragazzi, PagsGroup, LVMH Luxury Ventures Advisors, and the Hermès Family, Hulcan aims to integrate commerce, culture, media, and fashion in a single ecosystem. “We’re committed to preserving MATCHES’ legacy while transforming it for a new era of luxury,” said Maher. “This acquisition is foundational to building a connected, modern group that serves both brands and the next generation of luxury consumers.” Global asset advisory firm Gordon Brothers has acquired a majority interest in the intellectual property of the Rachel Zoe brand, aiming to accelerate its growth through expanded licensing, new product categories, and broader distribution. The investment solidifies Rachel Zoe’s evolution from celebrity stylist to influential lifestyle entrepreneur with a multi-channel media and consumer brand. Best known for her Bravo show The Rachel Zoe Project and editorial platform The Zoe Report, Zoe has built a business spanning apparel, home, fragrance, eyewear, and children’s products. She continues to lead the brand as Founder, Chief Creative Officer, and board member. “Rachel is a global fashion authority with a brand that resonates across style, media, and lifestyle,” said Tobias Nanda, Head of Brands at Gordon Brothers. “We’re excited to grow her legacy through strategic licensing and innovation.” Republic Brands Group (RBG) has acquired heritage fashion labels Joie, Equipment, and Current/Elliott for $36 million, forming a new division dubbed The Lux Group. The move marks a strategic expansion for RBG as it builds a portfolio of culturally resonant, commercially proven brands. RBG plans to pivot the labels from a retail-heavy model to a focus on DTC and wholesale, while expanding into new categories such as handbags, footwear, and accessories through licensing. The group will install new leadership and appoint dedicated creative directors for each brand. “We believe in the value and recognizability of these brands,” said CEO Sami Souid. “Each has an established customer base and a clear point of view that fits our long-term vision.” Republic Brands Group (RBG) has acquired heritage fashion labels Joie, Equipment, and Current/Elliott for $36 million, forming a new division dubbed The Lux Group. The move marks a strategic expansion for RBG as it builds a portfolio of culturally resonant, commercially proven brands. RBG plans to pivot the labels from a retail-heavy model to a focus on DTC and wholesale, while expanding into new categories such as handbags, footwear, and accessories through licensing. The group will install new leadership and appoint dedicated creative directors for each brand. “We believe in the value and recognizability of these brands,” said CEO Sami Souid. “Each has an established customer base and a clear point of view that fits our long-term vision.” Centric Brands has acquired Vingino Group, a Netherlands-based childrenswear label known for its denim-driven, multi-category fashion. The deal strengthens Centric’s international kidswear platform, leveraging Vingino’s deep retail relationships across Europe, Central America, and South America. Founded in 2001, Vingino offers styles for all ages anchored in craftsmanship and enduring design. “Vingino’s sourcing and design strength, plus their global network, align perfectly with our international growth strategy,” said Jason Rabin, CEO of Centric Brands. Vingino CEO Jan van den Berg added, “With Centric’s scale and expertise, we’re excited to accelerate our next chapter.” Prada S.p.A. has completed its acquisition of Versace from Capri Holdings for an enterprise value of €1.25 billion, following receipt of all required regulatory approvals. The deal sees Prada acquire 100 percent of Versace, marking a significant move in its strategy to bolster its position in the global luxury fashion market. The transaction, originally announced on April 10, 2025, follows months of exclusive negotiations and industry speculation. As part of the transition, Dario Vitale (formerly Miu Miu) assumed the role of creative director on April 1, succeeding Donatella Versace, who led the brand since 1997. Final deal value remains subject to customary closing adjustments related to Versace’s working capital and net debt. Prada Chairman Patrizio Bertelli emphasized shared values of “creativity, craftsmanship, and heritage,” while CEO Andrea Guerra noted the acquisition adds a “different and complementary dimension” to the group’s portfolio. Skims, the shapewear and apparel brand co-founded by Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede, has raised $225 million in a new funding round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, with participation from BDT & MSD Partners. The raise values the brand at $5 billion as it accelerates plans for product expansion, international growth, and a deeper push into physical retail. Launched in 2019, Skims has become a favorite among younger consumers thanks to its inclusive sizing, minimalist aesthetic, and Kardashian’s massive social media reach. The company, which expects to surpass $1 billion in net sales in 2025 and currently operates 20 retail locations across the U.S. and Mexico, will use the capital to grow its core intimates and shapewear lines, expand into apparel and activewear, and lay the foundation to become a retail-first business “This milestone reflects continued confidence in our long-term vision,” said CEO Jens Grede. “With disciplined execution, we’re ready to unlock Skims’ next phase of growth.” LVMH’s watch division has acquired a minority stake in Swiss movement manufacturer La Joux-Perret, strengthening a growing partnership aimed at advancing production and innovation across its watch brands, including TAG Heuer, Hublot, and Zenith. The strategic investment builds on existing collaborations between the two companies, including work on solar quartz movements for TAG Heuer and mechanical development for Tiffany & Co.’s Rope watch. Under the agreement, La Joux-Perret will remain fully independent, with Citizen Group retaining ownership of its watch brands. “Their technical mastery and deep roots in Swiss watchmaking make La Joux-Perret an ideal partner,” said Jean-Christophe Babin, CEO of LVMH Watches. The move comes as LVMH’s Watches & Jewelry division reported €7.41B in revenue for the first nine months of 2025, marking a 1% organic year-over-year increase. Global investment firm Carlyle has officially taken control of The Very Group, marking the end of the Barclay family’s more than 20-year ownership of the UK-based online retail giant. Abu Dhabi-based IMI, another major lender, remains a key stakeholder in the business. The Very Group, formerly Shop Direct and owner of Very.co.uk and Littlewoods, said the move provides a “strengthened capital base and enhanced financial flexibility” to support its long-term growth plans. Backers Carlyle and IMI, who have supported the group since 2021, will work with management to drive innovation and enhance the customer experience through tech and data investments. “This marks an important milestone as we enter a new phase of growth,” said CEO Robbie Feather. “Carlyle and IMI’s continued support gives us a stronger foundation to deliver on our strategy and build momentum.” Lingerie startup Peachaus has secured a £250,000 investment from retail veteran Angus Monro, the former CEO of Matalan, who also joins the company as acting Chairman. The funding marks a strategic milestone as Peachaus gears up for national expansion and future fundraising. Founded in 2022 by ex-Topshop Fashion Director Gillian Ridley Whittle, Peachaus is redefining lingerie retail through its values-led, direct-to-women model, bringing bra fittings to workplaces, co-working hubs, and festivals, rather than relying on traditional retail spaces. Monro joins a high-profile investor group that includes former Michael Kors CEO Cedric Wilmotte, ex-Wacoal CEO Tracey Lewis, and Sweaty Betty founder Tamara Hill-Norton, who are all backing Peachaus’ mission to build a sustainable, health-conscious brand poised to disrupt the global lingerie market. LuxExperience B.V., the digital luxury group behind Mytheresa, Net-a-Porter, and Mr Porter, has agreed to sell off-price fashion site The Outnet to The O Group LLC for $30 million. The deal includes all key assets, including brand rights, inventory, customer data, and U.S. distribution infrastructure, as well as the transfer of The Outnet’s U.S. and U.K. workforce. The Outnet, which specializes in discounted designer fashion from previous seasons, generated €260 million in net sales in FY25. While LuxExperience will retain a commercial relationship, continuing to supply merchandise and operational support, the sale marks a shift toward a leaner off-price strategy centered on Yoox. “The transaction will allow The Outnet to achieve its full potential under a renewed independent, stand-alone business model,” said Michael Kliger, CEO of LuxExperience. “It also enables us to accelerate transformation across our infrastructure and focus on driving growth at Yoox.” The deal is expected to close in Q1 2026, pending regulatory approvals. Homecourt, the luxury home care brand founded by Courteney Cox in 2022, has raised $8 million in Series A funding to scale its team, expand retail partnerships, and prepare for international growth. The round was led by Cult Capital with $5 million, alongside participation from existing investors and friends contributing the remaining $3 million. Known for its elevated home essentials, ranging from dish soap and surface sprays to candles and body care, Homecourt has reportedly reached $30 million in sales, with hand wash now leading in dollar volume. “Homecourt just means everything to me,” Cox said. “I needed partners who understood my obsession with detail and Cult Capital really got it.” With the investment, the brand plans to deepen its retail presence beyond Nordstrom and Bluemercury, grow its small but efficient team, and continue innovating around its best-selling CeCe fragrance line. International expansion is on the horizon, with London eyed as a potential launch point. “This brand works because I won’t settle for 99 percent,” Cox said. “It has to be perfect.” French e-commerce player Showroomprivé is divesting its 51% stake in fashion platform The Bradery, selling it back to founders Timothée Linyer and Edouard Caraco for €43.6 million. The move comes as part of a broader effort to streamline operations and strengthen the company’s financial position following a difficult fiscal year marked by a €39.7 million loss. Originally acquired in 2022 for €10.2 million, The Bradery has seen rapid growth, tripling its turnover from €21.7 million in 2021 to €62.9 million in 2024. Showroomprivé will receive an initial €17 million payment, with additional proceeds tied to performance-based milestones. The transaction is expected to close by year-end, pending regulatory approvals. Chalhoub Group has made a strategic minority investment in the menswear brand Willy Chavarria, joining existing investor FAE Fashion Ventures. The deal, reportedly under $5M, supports the label’s continued global expansion and infrastructure development. Chavarria, known for his culturally conscious, identity-driven collections, will benefit from Chalhoub’s deep operational expertise and regional retail presence across the Middle East. The investment follows a period of accelerated growth for the brand, which has tripled its wholesale footprint and launched collaborations with Adidas, Don Julio, and Tinder since FAE’s initial investment in 2024. The partnership marks Chalhoub’s continued evolution from distributor to brand builder, aligning with its broader strategy to back values-driven designers with long-term potential. Webster Capital has also joined the cap table alongside Chalhoub and FAE. “Together, we’re building a global powerhouse that connects with people where they are,” said Willy Chavarria. “Chalhoub and FAE bring the kind of integrity and cultural understanding that makes this partnership feel like family.” British retail giant Frasers Group has acquired a majority stake in The Webster, a high-end U.S. multi-brand luxury retailer known for its curated selection of over 100 designer labels, including Chanel, Dior, and Gucci. The Miami-based retailer has seen consistent growth, with a 10% increase in revenue and an expanded footprint of 13 boutiques across North America. Founder and CEO Laure Hériard Dubreuil will retain a minority stake and continue to lead operations. Calling the deal “the start of a new chapter,” Dubreuil praised the alignment between The Webster’s vision and Frasers Group’s ambition, especially around digital innovation and brand building. The acquisition supports Frasers Group’s elevation strategy, aimed at bolstering its luxury offering through its Flannels division, which already operates more than 80 stores in the UK and Ireland and maintains partnerships with brands like Moncler and Saint Laurent. Colorado-based outdoor brand Halfdays has raised $10 million in a Series A round led by Kellwood Company, with participation from Dick’s Sporting Goods Ventures, model Taylor Hill, and others. Known for redefining women’s skiwear with a stylish, functional edge, Halfdays was co-founded by Ariana Ferwerda, Karelle Golda, and Olympian Kiley McKinnon. The brand, which has gained traction over the past five years, is now shifting from survival mode to growth mode. “It’s the difference between surviving and scaling,” said Ferwerda, reflecting on the milestone moment. Fueled by strong seasonal performance and high sell-through rates, the funding will support expansion of Halfdays’ winter and ski lines, entry into year-round performance wear, accelerated wholesale partnerships with retailers like Revolve and Shopbop, and investments in brick-and-mortar retail. DK Company has acquired a majority stake in German fashion brand IVY OAK, expanding its presence in the premium fashion segment and strengthening its position in the German market. As part of the deal, IVY OAK’s headquarters will relocate to Copenhagen under DK Company’s structure, while the brand’s creative studio will remain in Berlin. “With IVY OAK, we see a perfect match between a strong, design-driven brand and DK Company’s expertise in international marketing and distribution,” said Jens Obel, CEO and co-owner of DK Company. “This acquisition supports our strategy of investing in the premium segment, while staying true to the creative and sustainable DNA of the brand.” German fashion label Closed has officially found new owners following insolvency proceedings. The Böck family, known for their role in Marc O’Polo, and fashion executive Dieter Holzer have acquired the company in a strategic move to revive the premium denim and lifestyle brand. Closed’s headquarters will remain in Hamburg, ensuring continuity for its operations and team. The acquisition secures the future of the brand, which has long been known for its high-quality craftsmanship and contemporary European aesthetic. Details of the restructuring plan or future strategy have not yet been disclosed, but the new owners are expected to focus on stabilizing operations, strengthening wholesale and retail presence, and rebuilding brand equity across core markets. Artistic Milliners has acquired a majority stake in Cone Denim from Elevate Textiles, forming a new multinational entity that will operate under the iconic Cone Denim name. The deal, set to close in Q1 2026, merges key assets from both companies while preserving Cone’s independent identity and leadership. The newly formed company will offer end-to-end denim solutions, with operations across Mexico, China, Pakistan, and the U.S., including Artistic Milliners’ SFI facility in Los Angeles and garment facility in Parras. “Combining Cone’s legacy with our global infrastructure creates a platform with unmatched scale, speed, and flexibility,” said Murtaza and Omer Ahmed of Artistic Milliners. VF Corporation has entered into a definitive agreement to sell iconic workwear brand Dickies® to Bluestar Alliance LLC for $600 million in cash. The deal marks a strategic portfolio move for VF and positions Dickies® for its next phase of growth under new ownership. Founded in 1922, Dickies® is a globally recognized brand known for blending utility and style, with a presence in 55 countries and deep cultural roots in both workwear and streetwear. “Dickies® has a rich legacy, and we’re excited to unlock its full potential,” said Bluestar Alliance CEO Joseph Gabbay. VF CEO Bracken Darrell added, “This transaction supports our strategy to strengthen our balance sheet and focus on core growth opportunities.” Kering and Mayhoola “ jointly announce that they have agreed to amend their shareholders’ agreement (initially concluded at the time of Kering’s acquisition of a 30% stake in Valentino in 2023) and more specifically the framework of the evolution of Valentino’s shareholding. According to this amendment, the current ownership structure of the House of Valentino will not change before 2028 at the earliest.” Premium sportswear brand Castore has acquired 100% of British heritage label Belstaff from INEOS, marking a major step in Castore’s expansion into the premium lifestyle category. As part of the deal, INEOS will also make a significant strategic investment at the Castore holding company level to support future global growth. Belstaff, known for its iconic waxed jackets and motorcycle-inspired fashion, will benefit from Castore’s direct-to-consumer expertise, global supply chain, and network of elite sports partnerships. “Belstaff is a truly iconic brand with unparalleled heritage,” said Castore CEO and Co-Founder Tom Beahon. “It’s a dream come true to lead it into its next chapter, and we’re equally thrilled to welcome INEOS as a strategic partner as we scale Castore globally.” Luxury skiwear and lifestyle brand Perfect Moment has secured $6.6 million in financing to support its next phase of growth. The funding includes a $5.1 million loan from chairman Max Gottschalk and a $1.5 million investment from X Cubed Capital Management, led by Andrew Redleaf. The capital will enable Perfect Moment to accelerate its expansion following recent strategic moves, including the opening of a new European distribution hub in the Netherlands and a corporate restructuring to boost operational efficiency and gross margins. “These financings demonstrate strong confidence in Perfect Moment’s strategy and brand potential,” said Gottschalk. “We’re now positioned to capitalize on growth opportunities through fiscal 2026 and beyond.” UK-based premium travel brand Antler has acquired US fashion-forward luggage label Paravel, forming the foundation of a new global strategy to build a ‘House of Travel Brands’ with projected sales surpassing £100 million by 2029. Paravel, which had previously filed for bankruptcy, will retain its brand identity under Antler’s leadership, with a full relaunch slated for 2026. The acquisition brings Antler, Nere (Australia), and Paravel under the ATR Group, each representing distinct market positioning and regional appeal. “This move strengthens our global reach and diversifies our portfolio across style, audience, and geography,” said Antler MD Kirsty Glenne. “With Antler, Nere, and Paravel under one roof, we’re well positioned to lead the next era of premium travel goods.” San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey has joined performance footwear and apparel brand while on earth™ as a co-founder and investor, marking a major milestone for the fast-growing company. Known for his longtime association with Nike, McCaffrey’s move signals a deep commitment to building a brand from the ground up. Launched in fall 2024, while on earth™ designs versatile, sustainably made footwear and apparel built for intentional movement between training and daily life. “For Christian to join us at this stage speaks volumes,” said founder Todd Meleney. “His involvement is already shaping our future, and we’re just getting started.” UK-based online fashion retailer Debenhams has secured a new three-year debt facility of up to £175 million, maturing in August 2028. The new funding replaces a prior £125 million credit line set to mature in October 2026 and follows a comprehensive market review led by CEO Dan Finley. The financing, led by TPG Angelo Gordon, carries an interest rate comprising the Bank of England base rate plus 7.3% and is designed to enhance the group’s financial flexibility as it executes a multi-year turnaround strategy. Earlier this year, the group rebranded from Boohoo to Debenhams, aligning its core brands, including Boohoo, PrettyLittleThing, and MAN, with the profitable Debenhams marketplace model. The company, which also owns Karen Millen, now operates an e-commerce platform offering around 15,000 brands. “We’ve put in place a new facility, 12 months early, with strong lenders that aligns with and supports our new strategy, supercharging Debenhams and turning around our youth fashion brands,” said Finley. Brand management firm Authentic has acquired a 51% stake in a newly formed entity that will own and license the majority of Guess’ global intellectual property. The remaining 49% will be retained by Guess cofounders Maurice and Paul Marciano, Nicolai Marciano, and CEO Carlos Alberini. The transaction adds approximately $6 billion in retail sales to Authentic’s portfolio, bringing its total annual global retail sales to $38 billion, making it the company’s second-largest brand acquisition after Reebok. As part of the deal, Guess and its subsidiaries will go private under current leadership, while Authentic focuses on expanding the brand into new categories and regions. “Guess is a powerhouse brand that’s shaped global style for decades,” said Authentic founder Jamie Salter. “We’re proud to partner with the Marciano family and build on their legacy as we take Guess into its next phase of growth.” Affordable luxury brand Quince confirmed on August 14 that it has raised $290 million in a Series D round at a valuation exceeding $4.5 billion, more than doubling its worth since a $120 million Series C round just six months ago. The San Francisco-based direct-to-consumer retailer, known for $50 cashmere sweaters and viral traction on Instagram and TikTok, continues to thrive even as other DTC players struggle. Iconiq Capital led the round with participation from DST Global, Notable Capital, Basis Set Ventures, and 8VC. “This milestone will help us accelerate our growth and continue delivering exceptional quality at radically fair prices,” the company said in a statement, adding that “what started with a $50 cashmere sweater has grown into a movement across apparel, home, beauty, wellness, and beyond. And we’re just getting started. Thank you to our customers, partners, and team for helping us get here.” The best is yet to come.” Canadian apparel maker Gildan Activewear has agreed to acquire U.S.-based Hanesbrands in a cash-and-stock deal valued at $2.2 billion, or about $6 per share, a 24% premium to Monday’s close. The acquisition will combine Hanesbrands’ branded retail portfolio, including Hanes, Bonds, Maidenform, and Playtex, with Gildan’s wholesale market strength across North America, Latin America, Asia-Pacific, and Europe. Citigroup analysts said the tie-up “makes sense on paper,” noting Gildan’s potential to manage Hanesbrands’ business more efficiently through its low-cost manufacturing expertise. Gemfields Group has sold luxury jeweller Fabergé Ltd to SMG Capital for $50 million as part of its strategy to streamline operations. Known for its ornate, jewelled eggs, Fabergé was acquired by Gemfields in 2012 to complement its coloured gemstone business and leverage the brand in jewellery marketing. The sale follows a strategic review launched late last year. Outzidr, the digital-first fashion brand catering to Gen Z women in India, has raised Rs 27 crore (approximately $3.1 million) in a pre-Series A round led by RTP Global, with participation from existing backer Stellaris Venture Partners. Founded in 2024, Outzidr launched in February 2025 with a trend-led western wear lineup targeting women aged 18–28. Known for its fast-paced test-and-scale model, the brand has already released over 8,000 styles and served 100,000+ customers in just five months, with retention rates 1.5x above industry benchmarks. The new capital will support Outzidr’s expansion into offline retail, with its first exclusive store set to open by March 2026, alongside investments in design, tech, and operations. “We’re building a brand that listens, learns, and reacts in real time,” said co-founder and CEO Nirmal Jain. Adanola, the U.K.-based cult womenswear brand redefining the active lifestyle wardrobe, has received a significant minority investment from Los Angeles-based private equity firm STORY3 Capital Partners. The deal, which values Adanola at approximately $530 million, marks a major milestone in the brand’s global growth journey. “This investment supports our vision to scale Adanola as a global leader in the active lifestyle category while building sustainable, profitable growth across key markets,” said CEO Niran Chana. The brand, known for its versatile, minimalist staples and celebrity fans like Kendall Jenner and Kaia Gerber, has sold over 1.5 million pairs of its signature Ultimate Leggings. Affordable luxury brand Quince has secured $200 million in fresh funding at a valuation exceeding $4.5 billion, more than doubling its worth since a $120 million Series C round just six months ago. The San Francisco-based direct-to-consumer retailer, known for $50 cashmere sweaters and viral traction on Instagram and TikTok, continues to thrive even as other DTC players struggle. Iconiq Capital led the round, bringing Quince’s total funding to date to $461.5 million. Founded in 2018, the company has expanded from clothing into luggage, furniture, and home goods – all while maintaining its factory-direct, sustainable model. Fashion-tech start-up ANNY has raised Rs. 10 crore ($1.15 million) in a Pre-Series A funding round led by early-stage investor Atomic Capital. Founded in 2003 by Japjot Singh (CEO), Aveen Kaur (COO), and Rahul Tanwar (CTO), ANNY operates a vertically integrated, inventory-light business model focused on trend-led fashion in the accessible luxury market in India. “With the support of Atomic Capital, we are not only scaling faster but also scaling smarter,” said Singh, adding that the investment will help fuel ANNY’s goal of becoming a Rs. 100 crore+ ARR brand by next year. Apoorv Gautam, Founder of Atomic Capital, praised ANNY’s operational excellence, strong consumer affinity, and capital-efficient growth trajectory. LVMH Luxury Ventures – the private equity arm of French luxury giant LVMH – has acquired a minority stake in Molli, the historic French knitwear house relaunched in 2014. The transaction marks the first external capital inflow for Molli since its revival by CEO Charlotte de Fayet and will support the brand’s international expansion plans. Founded in 1886 and renowned for its refined women’s knitwear and newborn essentials, Molli maintains production in France and Italy, working with heritage suppliers. In April, Molli opened a flagship store on Rue François 1er in Paris, designed as a template for future international locations. The new capital will be used to scale this retail concept, invest in knitting innovation, and expand the management team. “We’re proud to support Molli at this exciting stage of growth,” said a spokesperson for LVMH Luxury Ventures. “Its blend of heritage craftsmanship and contemporary positioning makes it a strong addition to our portfolio.” British luxury leather goods brand Mulberry has secured a £20 million capital injection from major shareholders Challice and Frasers Group to accelerate its transformation strategy amid a challenging luxury market. The fundraising comes as the company reported a 21% drop in annual revenues to £120.4 million and narrowed pre-tax losses to £31.8 million. The investment will support Mulberry’s “Back to the Mulberry Spirit” strategy, launched in January, which aims to return the brand to profitability through simplification, brand re-alignment, and international growth. Key initiatives include store optimisation in the UK and US, retail partnerships with Nordstrom and David Jones, and renewed product focus. CEO Andrea Baldo said the additional backing from shareholders reflects confidence in the brand’s vision, adding: “This is an ambitious transformation underpinned by operational discipline and creativity.” Heron Preston has reacquired full ownership of his namesake label, ending his partnership with Farfetch-affiliated New Guards Group. Reflecting on the path to regain his brand, Preston told BOF, “I have been through hell to protect what I have built. I fought for my name, my work and my vision. Now I am back with more purpose than ever.” Preston is preparing to relaunch the label in New York without any external investors. His next collection is expected to debut in October, following the conclusion of outside engagements, including his 2023 role as H&M’s creative advisor for menswear. Meta – the U.S. tech giant behind Facebook, Instagram, and Meta AI – has acquired a stake of just under 3 percent in EssilorLuxottica, the Italian-French eyewear conglomerate known for brands including Ray-Ban, Oakley, and Persol. The €3 billion investment deepens a partnership that began in 2019, focused on developing AI-powered smart glasses under the Ray-Ban Meta brand. EssilorLuxottica has sold over two million units of Ray-Ban Meta glasses since late 2023 and recently expanded the collaboration to include Oakley and luxury labels such as Prada. The company, which oversees a global supply chain and retail network, is expected to play a central role in Meta’s long-term hardware strategy. “This transaction reinforces Meta’s ambition to build its own hardware platform,” said a Meta spokesperson. “By investing in EssilorLuxottica, we are strengthening the foundation for the next generation of wearable AI experiences.” Saks Global Enterprises has secured a $600 million financing deal from a group of existing investors to ease mounting financial pressure just months after issuing $2.2 billion in debt to fund its Neiman Marcus acquisition. The agreement includes an immediate $300 million loan from majority bondholders, who gain repayment priority and avoid losses. The remaining $300 million will come through a debt swap, offering other lenders the option to exchange existing notes for lower-priority securities with the same 11% interest and 2029 maturity. Those who decline face subordination and the loss of key protections. DÔEN, a digitally native California lifestyle brand known for its feminine silhouettes, sustainability ethos, and women-led leadership, has closed a Series A funding round led by growth equity firm Silas Capital. Founded by sisters Margaret and Katherine Kleveland in 2016, DÔEN has scaled to $100M+ in revenue with minimal prior outside capital (~$1M). The new investment will support the brand’s retail expansion, infrastructure enhancements, and global customer engagement. With seven stores and strong wholesale/e-comm momentum (110% YoY wholesale growth, 40% e-comm growth), DÔEN is poised for continued omnichannel growth. “DÔEN is truly an exceptional brand – seamlessly blending its timeless appeal with product that offers both sophistication and practicality,” said Brian Thorne, Partner at Silas Capital. “We see tremendous potential to help grow their deeply loyal community by amplifying e-commerce momentum and further scaling the highly productive retail footprint. We are thrilled to partner with Margaret and Katherine at such a pivotal moment in their journey.” Footballer Erling Haaland and billionaire model Gustav Magnar Witzøe have joined Scandinavian luggage brand Db as strategic partners and minority investors. The new partnership follows LVMH Luxury Ventures Fund I (LLV) acquiring a minority stake in Db at the end of 2024. Haaland and Witzøe will work alongside LLV to support Db’s bold international expansion. Founded by Truls Brataas, Db designs travel gear at the intersection of sport, outdoor, adventure, and lifestyle. The company’s growing roster of partners reflects its ambition to build a global brand that resonates with a diverse and dynamic community of travelers. “We always look for like-minded people who share our ambitions, passion, and mindset. Erling and Gustav are two exceptional individuals who dare to dream big – they are a perfect match to Db,” said Truls Brataas, Founder at Db. Brittany-based Beaumanoir Group, owner of Cache Cache, Bonobo, Morgan, La Halle, and others, continues its European expansion with the acquisition of 26 Jennyfer stores. The deal will see the stores converted to Beaumanoir’s existing banners, while preserving approximately 350 jobs through a combination of retained and redeployed positions. The group will also acquire the Jennyfer brand name, planning a gradual relaunch aimed at a younger customer base, starting with Sarenza.com and later expanding to dedicated product lines across its retail network. The transaction complements a parallel deal by menswear retailer Celio, which is taking over seven additional Jennyfer stores to expand its Be Camaïeu concept. Beaumanoir and Celio jointly invested more than €2 million to complete the takeover, following Jennyfer’s recent restructuring efforts and struggles to modernize its brand in a highly competitive market. US billionaire Peter Kern, former vice-chairman and CEO of Expedia, has acquired Italian luxury lingerie label La Perla, securing both the brand rights and its Bologna production site. The acquisition, valued at approximately €25 million, was confirmed by Italy’s Ministry of Business and Made-in-Italy (MIMIT) and will safeguard 210 jobs, with plans for 40 additional hires. Although higher bids were submitted, Kern prevailed by committing to maintain La Perla’s manufacturing and product development in Bologna, preserving the brand’s Italian heritage and craftsmanship. “We’re committed to revitalizing La Perla by building on its deep expertise in luxury lingerie,” Kern stated. His wife, Kirsten, is said to have encouraged the acquisition. Kern will serve as La Perla’s new president, with Paolo Vannucchi returning as CEO to lead the brand’s turnaround. The relaunch will be supported by local advisory firm Studio Trombone, which is developing a long-term growth plan focused on leveraging Bologna’s historic production capabilities. Kontoor Brands, Inc. has officially completed its acquisition of Helly Hansen, the global outdoor and workwear brand, in a move aimed at accelerating growth and diversifying its category, channel, and geographic reach. “Today marks an exciting step forward for Kontoor as we expand our portfolio of iconic consumer brands,” said Scott Baxter, President, CEO, and Chairman of Kontoor Brands. “Helly Hansen brings strong global recognition and complements our strategic vision to strengthen our presence in the outdoor and workwear segments.” Storied Italian shoemaker Moreschi has been acquired by Glam Srl, the parent company of Superglamourous, and its backer, the London-based Imerman Family Office, following a court-supervised auction after Moreschi was declared bankrupt in 2024. The acquisition includes the Moreschi IP, machinery, and in-house materials. Founded in 1946 in Vigevano, Italy, Moreschi is best known for its luxury men’s formal shoes and enduring legacy in Italian shoemaking. The new owners will revive the brand by blending its heritage craftsmanship with Superglamourous’s digital-first capabilities. Manufacturing will remain in Italy, and both brands will operate independently while sharing backend infrastructure. “Our goal is to evolve Moreschi with thoughtful innovation, while preserving its core values of elegance and craftsmanship,” said Bianca Ladow, director of the Imerman Family Office and Glam Srl. The acquisition aims to position the duo for long-term growth in the modern luxury footwear market. Compagnie Chargeurs Invest – the French industrial group that serves as a supplier of leading apparel brands and the owner of the Swaine and The Cambridge Satchel Company brands – has raised €108 million in a new funding round involving four major credit institutions and additional bilateral loans. The financing includes participation from Groupe BPCE (Caisse d’Epargne Ile-de-France, Natixis, Banque Palatine), HSBC Continental Europe, La Banque Postale, and AG2R La Mondiale, along with renewable bilateral loans from Arkéa Banque and Bpifrance. “More than ever, we are in a position to increase the competitive advantage of our fast-growing global leaders,” said Fribourg. “This funding reflects the strength and long-term appeal of our model, underpinned by high-quality, high-value assets.” U.S.-based e-commerce powerhouse Revolve Group has acquired the intellectual property assets of Dion Lee, the Australian luxury label that shuttered operations late last year after entering insolvency. The acquisition, reportedly for under $1 million, marks a potential revival for the cult-favorite brand, with founder Dion Lee expected to remain as creative director. Revolve Group, which operates luxury fashion platforms Revolve and Fwrd, secured the brand’s assets following months of failed efforts by administrators to find a buyer. Dion Lee, once headquartered in Sydney and later based in New York, filed for bankruptcy in May 2024, burdened with $35 million in debt after key investor Cue Clothing withdrew support. Francesco Scognamiglio, the Neapolitan designer known for dressing icons like Madonna, Lady Gaga, and Beyoncé, has reacquired full ownership of his eponymous brand from Y Capital Management. The move marks the end of a creative hiatus that began in 2021, when diverging business visions led to the fund’s full takeover of the Francesco Scognamiglio and Maison Francesco Scognamiglio labels. “I’ve really wanted to take back what was essentially mine … These years have been a battle to buy back my creative freedom and voice,” said Scognamiglio. Now preparing for a relaunch, the designer will debut a 15-look couture collection in late June in Naples, ahead of Paris Couture Week. True Religion, the Los Angeles-based premium denim brand, has secured a strategic investment from Borletti Group, a firm known for its fashion and lifestyle holdings, including stakes in department stores Rinascente and Printemps. The deal brings together co-investors ACON Investments, Azimut, and the founders of Moose Knuckles. “This partnership will accelerate True Religion’s global development, with a focus on digital expansion and strengthening our omnichannel strategy,” the company stated. Founded in 2002, True Religion has evolved from a denim specialist to a full lifestyle brand, maintaining a strong presence across physical retail and e-commerce platforms. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. Skechers has entered into an agreement to be acquired by 3G Capital in a cash deal valuing the company at $63.00 per share—a 30% premium to its 15-day volume-weighted average stock price. The transaction will take Skechers private and marks a new chapter for the $9 billion global footwear brand, known for its comfort-focused innovation and accessible pricing. The company will continue to be led by Chairman and CEO Robert Greenberg, President Michael Greenberg, and COO David Weinberg. “With 3G Capital’s backing, we’re positioned to drive long-term growth while staying true to our mission,” said Greenberg. 3G Capital, known for its owner-operator model and investments in major consumer brands, emphasized its alignment with Skechers’ strategy and potential. Existing shareholders will also have the option to choose a mixed consideration alternative in lieu of the all-cash offer. Patrizio di Marco, former CEO of Gucci and Bottega Veneta, has acquired a minority stake in Be Sneakers, the Italian footwear manufacturer known for its role in reviving the Pro-Keds brand. Financial terms were not disclosed. Based in Barletta, Apulia, Be Sneakers reported €7.8 million in sales in 2024 (up 66% year-over-year) and is targeting €10 million in revenue for 2025. The company plans to leverage Di Marco’s global fashion expertise to expand its international reach and pursue high-profile collaborations. “I decided to join Be Sneakers because I found in this company a unique blend of cutting-edge technology, quality, and a truly Italian artisanal culture,” said Di Marco. “I strongly believe in its industrial and creative potential.” Swedish fashion group OJ Holding Sweden, parent company of Oscar Jacobson, has acquired minimalist fashion label Filippa K from investment firm Novax. The move brings together two iconic Scandinavian brands under one roof, with Filippa K set to operate independently within the group. Founded in 1993, Filippa K is renowned for its clean aesthetic and commitment to sustainability, generating SEK 436 million (approx. €38M) in turnover last year despite reporting a SEK 39 million (€3.4M) loss. “We are pleased with a new, experienced owner with deep knowledge of the sector,” said Filippa K CEO Marie Forssenius. OJ Holding CEO Richard Woodbridge added, “This acquisition aligns with our strategy to grow both organically and through selective investments.” The deal is expected to strengthen both brands’ market positions while preserving their unique identities. Xcel Brands (NASDAQ: XELB), a media and consumer products company specializing in influencer-driven brands, has announced a $9 million strategic investment and partnership with United Trademark Group (“UTG”). Known for its focus on live streaming and social commerce, Xcel will leverage UTG’s global expertise in brand development, licensing, and digital innovation to accelerate its next phase of growth. UTG brings deep experience in mergers, acquisitions, and operational infrastructure across design, manufacturing, distribution, and retail. “By combining their expertise in social commerce and our shared vision and commitment to product and innovation, we look forward to building the next generation of great brands,” said Alex Wang, Co-founder and Chairman of UTG. With this partnership, Xcel aims to unlock new growth opportunities through emerging media, experiential retail, and tech-driven brand experiences. The founders of Japanese fashion label Ambush, Yoon Ahn and Verbal, have reportedly reacquired full control of the brand from Italian fashion group New Guards Group. While financial terms have not been disclosed, the deal reverses New Guards Group’s majority acquisition of Ambush in 2020 and returns the label to independent ownership. The development follows a turbulent period for NGG, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in Italy in November 2024. Its parent company, Farfetch, was acquired by Coupang in late 2023, prompting multiple rounds of restructuring. Talks of a potential takeover of NGG by Style Capital earlier this year reportedly stalled without further progress. Prada Group will acquire 100 percent of Versace from Capri Holdings in a deal valued at €1.25 billion. The acquisition will bring the storied Italian fashion house under Prada’s ownership following months of industry speculation and exclusive talks between the two companies. Donatella Versace, who has led the house since her brother Gianni Versace’s death in 1997, recently vacated the creative director position, and Dario Vitale, formerly of Miu Miu, stepped into the role on April 1. The transaction remains subject to closing adjustments including the final price, which may be adjusted at or after closing based on estimates of Versace’s working capital and net debt. The deal is expected to close in the second half of the year and is part of a broader strategy to strengthen Prada Group’s position in the global luxury market. “ We are delighted to welcome Versace to the Prada Group and to build a new chapter for a brand with which we share a strong commitment to creativity, craftmanship and heritage,” said Patrizio Bertelli, Prada Group’s chairman and executive director. “We aim to continue Versace’s legacy celebrating and re-interpreting its bold and timeless aesthetic. At the same time, we will provide it with a strong platform, reinforced by years of ongoing investments and rooted in longstanding relationships.” “The acquisition of Versace marks another step in the evolutionary journey of our group, adding a new dimension, different and complementary,” Prada Chief Executive Officer Andrea Guerra said in a statement. Anta Sports has signed a deal to acquire German outdoor outfitter Jack Wolfskin from Topgolf Callaway Brands Corp. for $290 million. The transaction, subject to standard regulatory approvals, is expected to close by late Q2 or early Q3. “This sale will allow us to focus more on our core business and optimize our resources,” said Chip Brewer, president and CEO of Topgolf Callaway Brands. “It also strengthens our balance sheet ahead of the planned separation of Topgolf from our core operations.” The deal marks a strategic move for Anta as it continues expanding its portfolio of international performance and outdoor brands. The Very Group has completed a £598 million refinancing through the issuance of senior secured notes due August 2027, alongside an extension of its revolving credit facility to £150 million. The new structure replaces the online retail group’s former £50 million senior and £100 million super senior facilities, and pushes the maturity date of its senior term loan to August 1, 2027. “Our business is performing strongly as evidenced by our first half results, and today’s announcement allows us to focus on the continued delivery of our plan,” said Ben Fletcher, chief finance and transformation officer at The Very Group. “The refinancing demonstrates continued confidence from our partners, IMI and Carlyle.” Middle West Partners has acquired a majority stake in David Webb, the American jewellery house known for its bold designs and exceptional craftsmanship. Founded in 1948, the brand operates stores in New York, Beverly Hills, and Doha, and has built a loyal clientele drawn to its archival-rich, statement-making pieces. The investment, made alongside co-investor Pop Capital, signals a long-term growth strategy focused on expanding David Webb’s retail footprint, marketing efforts, and team. James Weiss, who has advised the company since 2017, has been appointed CEO. Former owner Mark Emanuel will retain a minority stake and remain actively involved in the business. UK-based Frasers Group has deepened its investment in Hugo Boss, expanding its stake in the German luxury fashion house through the sale of additional put options. The group now directly holds 13.5 million shares, representing a 19.2% stake, with the potential to raise its total holding to 23.7% if all options are exercised. Frasers’ maximum aggregate exposure to Hugo Boss stands at approximately €1.02 billion, based on the latest closing price. “This investment supports our strategy of building strong partnerships across the retail sector,” the company stated. As part of its growing involvement, CEO Michael Murray has been nominated for election to Hugo Boss’s supervisory board at its May 2025 general meeting, further cementing Frasers’ role as a strategic stakeholder amid shifting dynamics in the luxury market. UK high street giant New Look has landed a £30 million investment from shareholders to accelerate its digital transformation and sharpen its online customer experience. With eyes on the £4.3 billion UK online womenswear market, the retailer plans to double digital orders to £1 billion by 2030 and capture a 10% online market share by FY28. Already a category leader in dresses, outerwear, footwear, and denim, New Look boasts 300+ stores and over 10 million engaged customers. The new funding will fuel further personalisation, app optimisation, and digital upgrades—building on five years of tech investment, including a proprietary Enterprise Data Platform and a 7-million-strong social media following. True Classic, a fast-growing online menswear brand known for its affordable, high-quality basics, has received a strategic investment from 1686 Partners, the private equity firm launched by David Wertheimer. The funding marks True Classic’s first external capital raise since its founding in 2019 and values the company at approximately $850 million. With this new backing, the brand plans to strengthen its supply chain, scale up retail efforts, and expand its marketing reach to support continued growth in the competitive menswear space. Carlotta and Nicolò Oddi, co-founders of luxury Italian knitwear label Alanui, have regained full control of the brand after reacquiring the majority stake previously held by New Guards Group (“NGG”), the Milan-based fashion powerhouse owned by Farfetch. With this move, Alanui will now independently oversee all aspects of its operations and distribution, marking a significant shift as the brand charts its future course. Beginning with the S/S 2026 season, Alanui will manage direct distribution of its collections from a new Milan showroom. In a joint statement, the Oddis emphasized plans to bolster the brand’s global presence while maintaining the exquisite craftsmanship that defines Alanui’s identity. The transition follows financial instability at NGG, whose future became uncertain after Farfetch’s acquisition by Coupang and subsequent reports of unpaid royalties and bankruptcy protection proceedings in Italy. Purple Style Labs (“PSL”), India’s leading luxury fashion group, has secured $40 million in Series E funding led by SageOne, Alchemy Long Term Ventures, Bajaj Holdings & Investment, and Minerva Ventures. The round, including secondary investments, also drew participation from family offices, celebrities, and existing backers like Singularity Growth Fund and Pidilite Family Office. “This funding will accelerate our expansion in India and key global markets like New York, Los Angeles, and Dubai, while enhancing our omnichannel experience,” said founder Abhishek Agarwal. PSL is also set to open India’s largest multi-designer luxury store at the iconic Ismail Building in Mumbai. Exor, the holding company of Italy’s Agnelli family, has raised €3 billion ($3.14 billion) by selling a 4% stake in Ferrari. The sale is part of Exor’s strategy to reduce concentration in its investment portfolio and prepare for a “sizeable new acquisition when such an opportunity presents itself.” The company also plans to allocate part of the proceeds to a €1 billion share buyback program. Despite the sale, Exor remains Ferrari’s largest shareholder with a 20% stake and 30% of voting rights. Exor, which holds stakes in Stellantis and Philips, as well as controlling interests in Christian Louboutin, Iveco, CNH, and Juventus, will use the majority of the proceeds from this sale to broaden its portfolio with a significant new acquisition. John Elkann, CEO of Exor and Chairman of Ferrari, reaffirmed Exor’s commitment, stating, “Our commitment to remain Ferrari’s largest shareholder for the long term is stronger than ever.” Tapestry, Inc. has entered into a definitive agreement to sell the Stuart Weitzman brand to Caleres, a market-leading portfolio of consumer-driven footwear brands, for $105 million in cash, subject to customary adjustments. The transaction is expected to close in the summer of 2025, subject to customary closing conditions. Update (Aug. 4, 2025) : Caleres  closed on the acquisition of Stuart Weitzman from Tapestry, Inc. for $120.2 million, which included $11.5 million in cash received at the closing. Excluding cash received at the closing, the net purchase price was $108.7 million. The purchase price is subject to final adjustments for net working capital. Ahlem, the luxury eyewear brand headquartered in Los Angeles, has secured an undisclosed investment from Luxembourg-based private equity firm 1686 Partners, which specializes in purpose-driven lifestyle companies. The funding will support Ahlem’s global expansion, enhancing its retail presence, client services, wholesale operations, marketing initiatives, and production capacity. The investment follows the appointment of Enrico Sanavia as Global CEO, who aims to double Ahlem’s business within three years and establish it as “the most recognized and respected luxury eyewear company in the world.” Ahlem Manai-Platt, founder and creative director, emphasized the shared vision with 1686 Partners, stating, “We share the same priority: To build a meaningful and enduring legacy.” Steve Madden Ltd. has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Kurt Geiger London from a group led by international private equity firm Cinven for an enterprise value of approximately 289 million pounds ($360 million). London-headquartered Kurt Geiger’s brand portfolio includes KG Kurt Geiger and Carvela and also operates footwear concessions within luxury and premium department stores in the United Kingdom. “We are thrilled to be adding Kurt Geiger London, a brand that has experienced exceptional growth in recent years, with this acquisition,” said Edward Rosenfeld, CEO of Steve Madden. “Its differentiated and aspirational positioning in the market – coupled with its alignment with our strategic initiatives to expand in international markets, the accessories category, and direct-to-consumer channels – makes this a highly attractive and complementary addition to our portfolio.” Bluestar Alliance LLC has acquired Palm Angels from New Guards Group. The terms of the deal have not been disclosed. The acquisition of Palm Angels, a 10-year-old luxury streetwear brand, follows Bluestar Alliance’s recent acquisition of Off-White from LVMH, and “underscores Bluestar Alliance’s continued expansion into the high-end streetwear and luxury fashion sectors,” the group said. “We are thrilled to welcome Palm Angels into the Bluestar Alliance brand portfolio,” said Joey Gabbay, CEO of Bluestar Alliance. “The brand’s unique ability to bridge the worlds of streetwear and luxury has set it apart in the fashion industry. Amazon – which will work with Saks Global “to offer its expertise in logistics and personalization technology” – will hold a minority stake in the new entity, as will cloud-based software company, Salesforce. “For years, many in the industry have anticipated this transaction and the benefits it would drive for customers, partners and employees,” Richard Baker, HBC executive chairman and CEO, said in a statement. “This is an exciting time in luxury retail, with technological advancements creating new opportunities to redefine the customer experience, and we look forward to unlocking significant value for our customers, brand partners and employees.” “The deal should help reduce operating costs and create more negotiating power with vendors. LVMH has acquired Switzerland-based speciality clock maker L’Epee 1839 and its owner and its owner Swiza. The terms of the deal have mot been disclosed. L’Epee will be housed within LVMH’s growing Watches division , which is led by Frédéric Arnault. “L’Épée 1839 is at once a beautiful brand with a history that dates back to 1839, internationally recognized and by an audience of watchmaking enthusiasts, but most of all, it has a unique know-how,” Arnault said in a statement. “It is the only one to do what its teams do in the industry and has regrouped under one roof an impressive diversity of crafts.” The deal comes as LVMH looks to expand the range of its luxury goods offerings, including by “boosting its expertise in high-end watch making.” Revolve Group, Inc. has acquired a majority stake in Alexandre Vauthier, confirming that it will invest six million euros ($9.67 million) over the next three years in the ailing French fashion brand, which was placed in administration last year and has been actively seeking a buyer. Revolve co-CEO Michael Mente said in a statement, “By integrating our impactful brand marketing strategies and operational excellence with Vauthier’s visionary designs, we are set to ignite a new era of fashion influence in luxury to build an iconic French maison.” Bernard Arnault has taken a stake in Richemont, according to industry reports. Details regarding the LVMH chairman and CEO’s position, which he has taken on in a personal capacity, are sparse, with Bloomberg reporting that the size of the holding is “small” and part of a broader Arnault family-owned portfolio of investments in publicly listed companies. Daydream has raised a $50 million in a Seed round co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Index Ventures with participation from GV (Google Ventures) and True Ventures. Couper, a luxury fashion retailer that features “thoughtfully designed exclusive collaborations from emerging global designers,” has acquired Sovereign Collective, a luxury e-commerce platform that provides “unparalleled curation of the best styles and trends from global designers.” The terms of the deal have not been disclosed. Agee Leinberry-founded Couper said in a statement, “We are thrilled to announce that Couper has officially acquired Sovereign Collective, a like-minded, multi-brand platform featuring emerging contemporary designers from around the world. We very much look forward to working together to realise the full potential of this exceptional Maison within the thriving branded jewellery market.” Richemont revealed that the transaction will have “no material financial impact on Richemont’s consolidated net assets or operating result for the year ending 31 March 2025.” Frasers Group confirmed that it has reached a deal with the administrators of MATCHES to buy back “certain intellectual property assets” from the bankrupt online fashion platform, which it acquired (as a whole) from Apax Partners in December 2023 and put into administration in the United Kingdom in March 2024. The Milan-based online fashion retail platform, which offers a curated selection of luxury brands, including a mix of new and pre-loved items, will use the new funds to expanding its physical retail footprint, grow its the team, and grow its presence in new markets beginning in 2025. Qlhype founder and CEO Simone Marini said, “From the digital world we continue to bring the Qlhype experience to physical stores, and in 2025, our goal is to export our model internationally.” Konvi, a European luxury assets fractional investment platform, has acquired alternative investing platforms Diversified and Fractible. The terms of the deals have not been disclosed. The three companies facilitate fractional investments in luxury items, including high-end handbags, artworks, fine wines, whiskeys, watches, and vintage cars. Konvi co-founder and CEO Eran Peer said, “Acquiring Diversified and Fractible, both leading luxury investment platforms in France, is a crucial step in strengthening Konvi’s position as the European leader in this market. The terms of the deal have not been disclosed. The companies said in a statement that the merger “brings together Knot Standard’s advanced technology and client experience with Billy Reid’s strong national presence. Speaking of his new investment venture, the former Gucci CEO, who will be appointed chairman of Bologna, Italy-based Elisabetta Franchi, said in a statement that “this new chapter of my professional life will focus on investments in valuable companies and human resources.” His investments will focus on companies in the fashion and luxury sector in Italy and abroad. Italy’s Rivetti family confirmed that it has sold off a 1.18 percent stake in Moncler through an accelerated book-building to institutional investors at 67 euros per share. The news “comes less than a month after the announcement that the Rivetti family” – the former owner of Stone Island, the Italian luxury men’s fashion and outerwear brand acquired by Moncler in December 2020 in a $1.4 billion deal – “would become a direct shareholder in the luxury group after ending an investment agreement with [Moncler] CEO Remo Ruffini’s holding company Double R,” per Reuters. The Rivettis still hold 0.5 percent of Moncler share capital. Miroglio finalized its acquisition of Trussardi in a deal that saw it paid 35 million euros ($38.28 million) for the assets of the more than 100-year-old Italian luxury brand, per Reuters. Miroglio, an Italian firm specializing in the manufacture and distribution of apparel, said the deal will enable Trussardi to remain an independent brand and enable Miroglio to expand into menswear and leather goods. Miroglio CEO Alberto Racca said in a statement that the deal is “a key step in our strategy of growth and portfolio diversification.” Milan-based private equity investor Style Capital will acquire a 50.2 percent stake in Italian sneaker brand Autry from fellow Italian private equity firm Made in Italy Fund for an undisclosed sum. The Door family, which is the founding shareholder in Autry, will retain a “significant” holding in the company. Meanwhile, Reuters reports that Quadrivio & Pambianco, which owns the Made in Italy Fund, will reinvest in Autry via another, as-of-now unnamed fund. Under Style Capital’s ownership, Autry plans to increase its expansion in Italy and abroad, including by opening more than 20 mono-brand stores. The Very Group has raised a £125 million in a new round, with Carlyle putting in £85 million of the funds and IMI investing the remaining £40 million. The Barclay family-owned retail group, which owns/operates Littlewoods.com and Very.co.uk, as well as Very Financial Services, will use the new funds to “support its growth strategy.” Acting non-executive chair Aidan Barclay said that with the new funds from Carlyle and IMI, the group has “the support of two long-term, experienced institutional sponsors that understand our business extremely well. Luxury ski and outerwear company Perfect Moment Ltd. offered just upwards of 1.33 million shares in its public debut on the NYSE American exchange . Trading opened on February 8 at $4.43. The London-headquartered company, which describes itself as “a luxury lifestyle brand that combines fashion and technical performance for its ranges of skiwear, outerwear, swimwear and activewear,” has granted the underwriters a 45-day option to purchase up to an additional 200,100 shares of common stock to cover over-allotments, if any, at the public offering price, less the underwriting discount. SIXTY PERCENT has raised 460 million yen ($3.1 million) in a Series A funding round led by Global Brain’s Kuroneko Innovation Fund, an existing investor, with participation from Ambush co-founder Verbal. The Tokyo-based e-commerce platform, which connects Asian fashion brands with Japanese consumers, says it will use the new funds to “achieve further business expansion with [the help of] Yamato Holdings Co., Ltd., the Limited Partner of KURONEKO Fund.” The company says that it has been established as a “unique cross-border e-commerce solution” that offers a wide range of features all in one place including multi-language assistance, logistics, payment, and customer service. Reflo has raised £1 million in a Seed round with participation from England football star Harry Kane. The Doncaster, England-based “sustainable” performance-wear brand says that its offerings – which “focus on sustainability, performance, and style, specializing in golf but also catering for gym goers, runners and other sports like tennis and padel” – are “predominantly made from recycled polyester, derived from single-use plastic waste destined for landfill which results in its fabrics using 50% less energy and producing 70% less carbon than virgin polyester, requiring no new oil.” It will use the new funds to support its production and business operations, particularly in material sourcing, staff, and production factory choices. Coupang has finalized its acquisition of Farfetch Holdings plc , confirming that Farfetch “will continue delivering exceptional services for its brand and boutique partners.” WWD cited sources as saying that negotiations to sell non-core assets in the Farfetch portfolio, such as Browns and New Guards Group, “are ongoing,” and that Farfetch founder Jose Neves “is on leave, and it remains unclear when he will return to the business.” Newme has raised Rs 45 crore ($5.4 million) in a Seed funding round led by Fireside Ventures with participation from Aum Ventures, 2am VC, and All In Capital. Newme’s co-founder and CEO Sumit Jasoria said the company will use the new funds to “enhance our supply chain and scale-up the manufcaturing in [India], go from 2 to 20 cities in our offline play and build a stronger tech team over the course of the coming 12 months.” It will also use a portion of the proceeds to hire more individuals in leadership roles. Singer Harry Styles has taken a minority stake in British menswear brand S.S. Daley. Founder Steven Stokey-Daley, who confirmed the funding on January 11, said, “It’s been very much organic. Daley and we look forward to this new chapter together as we focus on brand longevity and scaling the business into a modern British heritage house.” Frasers Group will acquire luxury clothing retailer Matches Fashion in a £52 million ($66 million) deal. Absolute Brands has raised $2.5 million in a Seed funding round led by Capstone Ventures with participation from a number of angel investors. WWD reports that “a further funding round already slated for 2024 meant to accelerate [the brand’s] retail projects.” Kering announced that it has completed the acquisition of a 30 percent shareholding in Valentino, “in accordance with the terms disclosed on July 27, 2023, and following clearance from the antitrust authorities.” The stake “will be accounted for using the equity method, starting from [November 30] onwards,” Kering said in a statement . British premium sportswear Castore has raised £150 million in a round led by The Raine Group with participation from Hanaco Ventures and Felix Capital. The FT reports that the round, which is the largest in Castore’s history, values the company at £950 million after taking the new money into account, citing a person with knowledge of the matter. Shein has confidentially filed to go public in the U.S. “The retailer was last valued at $66 billion and could be ready to start trading on the public markets as soon as 2024,” people familiar with the matter told CNBC. Meanwhile, Reuters reports that Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley have been hired as lead underwriters for the IPO. Adrian Cheng has taken a majority stake in 1017 Alyx 9SM , the label launched in 2015 by current Givenchy creative director Matthew Williams. Urbanic has raised $150 million in a Series C funding round from Switzerland’s Mirabaud Lifestyle Impact and Innovation Fund, New York-based public-private hybrid investment firm D1 Capital Partners, JAM Fund and other global investors and European luxury fashion families. Previous backers include Nexus Venture Partners and Sequoia Capital. The London, UK-based fashion brand will use thew new funds to “support [its] mission to transform the fashion industry by leveraging AI and machine learning-based models, which are supported by its proprietary large language model that is trained on a variety of codebases to “systematically generate fashion designs, AIGC-based creatives and content, and improve overall supply chain efficiency to the next level for the fashion industry.” Founder James Wellwood said in a statement, “We will continue to leverage groundbreaking technology and partnerships with manufacturers and suppliers who comply with the highest standard of international working conditions that protect our people and our planet. Mike Ashley-led Frasers said on Monday that Chinese ultra-fast fashion titan Shein will acquire the intellectual property of Missguided, while it will retain its real estate and employees, which have been integrated into Frasers’ growing fashion division. Financial details of the deal have not been disclosed. Shein also revealed that it has “signed an agreement to license the Missguided brand IP to Sumwon Studios, a joint venture between Shein and Missguided’s founder Nitin Passi, which will manage the brand,” per the WSJ. “Missguided’s products and collections will be manufactured through Shein’s on-demand production model and sold on its sites and on Missguided.com as an independent brand.” “This move is particularly noteworthy because it marks Shein’s first acquisition of a British brand, aligning well with its focus on the UK as one of its fastest-growing markets,” Shore Capital analyst Eleonora Dani told Reuters. Engaged Capital has built a position in apparel brand owner VF Corp, arguing that the Denver, Colorado-headquartered company is mismanaged and that its stock price could triple if those issues are addressed. Engaged Capital’s Chris Hetrick said the company’s business “can likely be turned around and said the North Face brand is very healthy globally and that the Vans brand has lost ‘heat’ but can be repaired,” per Reuters. Hetrick, an activist investor, further said that VF, which owns North Face, Eastpak, Timberland, Vans, Jansport, and Supreme, among other brands, “should evaluate boosting its non-core asset divestment program as well as consider taking offers for all the company’s brands except Vans and The North Face.” Frasers Group has signed a binding agreement to acquire SportScheck, one of the leading sports retailers in Germany, from Signa Retail Department Store Holding GmbH. The financial terms of the transaction have not been disclosed. SportScheck generates an estimated €350 million ($369.6 million) in annual revenue from its network of 34 stores in cities across Germany. Frasers Group CEO Michael Murray said: “Acquiring the leading sporting goods retailer in Germany is a big step in our journey to becoming the number one sports retailer in EMEA – and we are delighted to do this with the full support of major global brand partners, adidas and NIKE. Growing and expanding our Sports business is a key focus area in becoming an international retail business. The Mike Ashley-run retail group now holds 15.1 percent of the voting rights in Boohoo, up from 13.4 percent. “Frasers has also been picking up shares in other UK retailers, with the latest move likely to stoke speculation on whether it is just taking advantage of undervalued stocks or there is more to its actions,” per Bloomberg. Aside from Next confirming that it will put up a combination of cash and new Next shares in furtherance of the deal, the terms have not been disclosed. Birkenstock offered up 10.75 million ordinary under the ticker “BIRK.” L Catterton – the private equity group backed by French billionaire Bernard Arnault and LVMH that acquired a majority stake in Birkenstock in 2021 – offered 21.5 million. Neso Brands CEO Bjorn Bergstrom said in a statement that “this strategic investment marks our first foray into the European market.” Birkenstock announced on September 12 that it will list shares on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker BIRK – without disclosing how many shares it will list or what the anticipated price range for those shares will be. It did, however, reveal that its net revenue for the six months ending on March 31 amounted to 644.17 million euros ($692.87 million), up 19 percent, and its profit was 40.21 million euros (down 45.3 percent). Private equity firm Advent has acquired a majority stake in Zimmermann from founder-sisters Nicky and Simone Zimmermann and the Milan-based Style Capital fund (the latter of which acquired an estimated 70 percent stake in 2016 from American private equity firm General Atlantic), in a deal that reportedly values the Australian fashion brand at $1.5 billion. SKIMS co-founder and CEO  Jens Grede told The New York Times DealBook that the company expects to generate $750 million in sales in 2023, up from $500 million in 2022. As for the company’s plans, “At some point in the future, Skims deserves to be a public company,” he said. Musinsa raised 240 billion won ($189.7 million) in its Series C round from a consortium led by global private equity giant KKR & Co. Inc., with participation from U.S. investment firm Wellington Management Co. South Korea’s leading fashion platform, Musinsa will use the new funds to “strengthen its profitability, secure the intellectual property of overseas fashion brands that haven’t yet entered the Korean market and invest in promising designer brands.” The 22-year-old company – which reported revenues of 708.3 billion won in 2022, up 53.6 percent year-over-year, but operating profits of 3.2 billion won (down 94.6 percent YoY) and net losses of 55.8 billion won – will also expand its existing pop-up stores in the Seongsu, Hannam and Hongdae areas in Seoul, while opening more Musinsa Standard stores and boutiques in Daegu and Busan. Blk Dnm has been acquired by ChromaWay, marking the first fashion industry acquisition by the Swedish blockchain developer. The terms of the deal, which was first reported by WWD, were not disclosed.
