Puck reported that holders of Everlane common stock are not expected to receive proceeds from the transaction, though details regarding preferred shareholders were not disclosed. The acquisition would give Shein ownership of a well-known U.S. contemporary fashion label as the company continues expanding beyond its fast-fashion roots and deepening its global retail footprint. LVMH has agreed to sell Marc Jacobs to a joint venture formed by WHP Global and G-III Apparel Group, with the buyers raising up to $850 million to finance the acquisition. Under the deal, WHP Global and G-III will each contribute up to $425 million, with WHP overseeing licensing operations and G-III managing the brand globally. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. The sale marks the end of LVMH’s nearly 30-year ownership of Marc Jacobs, which it acquired in 1997. Founder Marc Jacobs will remain creative director following the transaction. The acquisition expands WHP Global’s premium fashion portfolio, which already includes Vera Wang, rag & bone, and G-STAR, while reflecting broader consolidation trends in the accessible luxury market. Castore has secured a £90 million credit facility from HSBC UK, BNP Paribas, and Lloyds to support retail expansion in the UK and accelerate growth across key international markets in the Middle East and Asia. The Manchester-based sportswear brand plans to use the financing to expand its store footprint and strengthen its position as a global premium performance apparel company. Castore is targeting more than £300 million in sales over the next financial year. “This new funding provides us with the flexibility and ability to accelerate our retail rollout,” said co-founder Tom Beahon. Founded in 2015, Castore has attracted backing from investors including Andy Murray and INEOS, and recently acquired heritage fashion brand Belstaff for approximately £102 million. Kering has announced it will acquire a minority stake in Shanghai-based Icicle Fashion Group as part of a strategic partnership with its parent company ICCF. Founded in 1997, Icicle is a fast-growing Chinese luxury brand with more than 200 stores globally, including a presence in Paris, and has been expanding into Western markets. The investment reflects Kering’s continued focus on strengthening its position in China while supporting the international growth of local luxury brands. Financial terms were not disclosed. Kering and L’Oréal have finalized their strategic beauty partnership, confirming L’Oréal’s €4 billion acquisition of Kering Beauté, including the House of Creed, along with long-term fragrance and beauty licenses for Kering’s luxury Houses. The agreement also includes plans to explore new opportunities in wellness and longevity through a joint venture, signaling a broader expansion beyond traditional beauty categories. “Our strategic alliance with L’Oréal marks a decisive step forward for Kering,” said CEO Luca de Meo. For L’Oréal, the deal strengthens its leadership in luxury beauty, building on its longstanding success with brands like Yves Saint Laurent Beauté while unlocking new growth opportunities across Kering’s portfolio. Perfect Moment has secured $12 million in growth financing to strengthen its balance sheet and support its path to sustainable profitability. The package includes a $10 million revolving credit facility from Krane Capital and X3 Higher Moment Fund, alongside a $2 million equity investment from Krane Capital, priced at a 75% premium to the company’s recent share price. The funding follows the brand’s first profitable quarter and will be used to enhance liquidity, invest in product innovation, and expand into new categories and markets. A key focus is China, where Krane Capital’s local expertise is expected to support distribution and market entry within the premium segment. “This financing enhances our financial flexibility and supports continued expansion across our key initiatives,” said Executive Chairman Max Gottschalk. American Exchange Group has agreed to acquire the assets of Allbirds in a $39 million deal, marking a dramatic reset for the once high-flying sustainable footwear brand. The transaction, expected to close in Q2 2026 pending shareholder approval, will include the winding down of Allbirds’ public company structure. The deal follows a sharp decline in performance, with the company reporting a 23.3% drop in quarterly revenue and continued losses, alongside the closure of its remaining U.S. stores. Originally launched in 2016 and once valued at over $4 billion, Allbirds rose quickly on the strength of its minimalist wool sneakers before struggling with rapid expansion and strategic missteps. “This next chapter… sets up the brand to thrive in the years ahead,” said CEO Joe Vernachio. For American Exchange Group, the acquisition adds to a growing portfolio of fashion and lifestyle brands, signaling continued consolidation in the footwear and apparel sector. Sandbridge Capital, a private equity firm focused on consumer and luxury investments, has taken a 5% stake in  Jacquemus. The transaction involves the sale of the founder’s personal shares, rather than new capital being injected into the business. It follows L’Oréal’s earlier investment of around 10%, supporting Jacquemus’ planned expansion into beauty, including a cosmetics line set to launch in 2027. Despite new investors, founder Simon Porte Jacquemus retains majority ownership. London-based fashion distributor and brand incubator Tomorrow Ltd. has been acquired by Progetto 11, the parent company of Italian e-commerce platform The Level Group. Financial terms were not disclosed, though existing investor Three Hills Capital Partners is reported to have taken a loss on its stake. Founded as a showroom business, Tomorrow evolved into a brand incubator with stakes in labels including Coperni and Martine Rose, supporting production, development, and distribution. However, the company has faced mounting challenges in recent years, including declining revenues, liquidity pressures, and tensions with partner brands. “The focus of the board has been to guarantee protection and continuity for the business,” said founder Stefano Martinetto. The acquisition is expected to stabilise operations and integrate Tomorrow into The Level Group’s broader e-commerce and logistics platform, though the future of its brand partnerships remains uncertain. French rainwear brand Flotte has raised €2.5 million in funding from Time4, a new investment fund launched by Daphni and Les Déterminés. The funding will support the brand’s growth and expansion as it continues to scale its sustainable outerwear offering. Founded as a specialist rainwear label, Flotte focuses on functional, eco-conscious apparel designed for urban lifestyles. Online retailer Quince has raised $500 million in a Series E funding round led by ICONIQ Capital, with participation from Basis Set Ventures and Wellington Management. The round values the company at $10.1 billion. The San Francisco–based platform sells apparel, jewelry, and home goods through a manufacturer-to-consumer model that removes traditional retail intermediaries. Its AI-driven platform forecasts demand and produces goods in smaller batches to reduce excess inventory. Quince reported more than $1 billion in revenue in 2025 and plans to use the new funding to support global expansion of its technology-enabled retail model. Frasers Group has acquired a 5.8% stake in German sportswear company Puma, according to regulatory filings. The position was largely built through derivatives tied to roughly 8.5 million shares. If exercised, the stake would make Frasers Puma’s second-largest shareholder behind the Pinault family. The move follows Anta Sports’ agreement earlier this year to purchase a 29% stake in Puma for €1.5 billion. Puma is a major supplier to Frasers’ Sports Direct chain, and the investment further expands Frasers’ portfolio of minority stakes in European fashion and retail brands. Private equity firm FSI is set to become the controlling shareholder of Italian luxury brand Missoni with a 73% stake, as the Missoni family exits its equity position. Katjes International will also acquire a 27% stake through its subsidiary Katjes Quiet Luxury. The transaction, expected to close in Q2 pending regulatory approval, positions FSI as the majority owner while giving Katjes the option to increase its stake in the future. Missoni CEO Livio Proli will remain in his role as the brand continues its growth strategy. Dallas-based private equity firm Trive Capital has made a strategic investment in women’s occasionwear brand Adrianna Papell. Financial terms were not disclosed. Founded in 1980 and headquartered in New York, Adrianna Papell designs cocktail, evening, and daywear styles and has sold more than 40 million dresses globally. The brand distributes through direct channels and retail partners across 27 countries. With Trive’s backing, the company plans to expand into new product categories, grow its direct-to-consumer and international presence, and pursue strategic acquisitions. The existing management team will continue to lead the business. Ashley Stewart has secured $15 million in new funding to support its next phase of growth and operational expansion. The plus-size fashion retailer plans to use the capital to strengthen its digital capabilities, enhance customer experience, and invest in strategic initiatives aimed at long-term brand development. The funding reinforces Ashley Stewart’s position in the inclusive fashion market as it continues to focus on omnichannel growth and deeper engagement with its core customer base. Outopia, a Chinese outdoor performance brand co-founded by a former Lululemon executive, has closed a Series B funding round led by Meridian Capital (Huaying Capital), with participation from Challenjers Venture, Ventech China, and Shunwei Capital. Financial terms were not disclosed. Founded in 2021 by Aaron Jackson, former director of raw material innovations and advanced concepts at Lululemon, and Alexis Hou, a former LVMH Asia-Pacific executive, Outopia specializes in technical merino wool apparel focused on trail running. The brand operates in China, New Zealand, and Australia. The company has built recognition around its performance fabrics and functional design, positioning itself within the professional trail running segment while expanding its offline retail footprint and overseas presence. Investors highlighted Outopia’s combination of technical innovation and strong brand identity as key drivers of its growth trajectory. Debenhams Group has increased its planned capital raise from £35 million to £40 million, aiming to strengthen liquidity and optimize its capital structure as it advances its restructuring and growth plans. The new shares were issued at 18 pence each, representing a 5% discount to the February 17 closing price of 19 pence. The company is also in discussions with lenders regarding amendments to its debt facilities. “The increase will provide an improved capital structure and greater financial flexibility to execute the restructuring and generate value,” said CEO Dan Finley. The raise involves senior leadership, including Finley and co-founder and executive chairman Mahmud Kamani. Non-executive director Iain McDonald resigned with immediate effect following nine years with the company. Aritzia has acquired the Fred Segal brand from Fred Segal Family LLC. Financial terms were not disclosed. As part of the deal, the Vancouver-based retailer has also leased 8100 Melrose Avenue in Los Angeles, the brand’s original flagship location. The move supports Aritzia’s long-term U.S. expansion strategy while marking an effort to revive the storied California lifestyle label. Founded in 1961, Fred Segal became synonymous with “California cool,” pioneering experiential retail and serving as a cultural hub for fashion, celebrities, and television. The brand helped shape Los Angeles’ style identity for decades. “Fred Segal has long been a cultural touchstone in Los Angeles, a place where creativity, community and style converge,” said Aritzia CEO Jennifer Wong. “We are honored to steward and evolve this iconic brand for a new generation with the elevated experience and ‘everyday luxury’ that define Aritzia.” Aritzia plans to restore the Melrose property, including its signature ivy-covered façade, and transform the space into a new experiential retail destination combining curated product and immersive lifestyle elements. The acquisition follows Aritzia’s previous investment in menswear brand Reigning Champ, signaling its continued appetite for strategic brand expansion as it grows its U.S. footprint. The Very Group has extended and renewed its main debt facilities, securing funding through 2029 and 2030 after Carlyle became its controlling shareholder last year. Its £1.77 billion securitization facility has been extended to February 2029, and its £150 million revolving credit facility now runs to February 2030. Ratings on the securitisation notes were confirmed or upgraded by Fitch and DBRS. The company also reduced its overall debt by £150 million with support from Carlyle. The interest rate on its senior secured notes has been lowered from 13.5% to 9.75%, and their maturity extended to August 2030. CFO Edward Fry said the deal strengthens the balance sheet and gives the business a stable base for future growth and investment. Frasers Group is set to acquire a majority shareholding in Maxi Sport SpA, the Italian activewear and sporting goods retailer. The founding Sala family will retain a minority stake and continue in leadership roles as the business enters its next phase of growth. Founded in Italy, Maxi Sport operates 18 stores nationwide, including six flagship locations, and offers a broad assortment across premium sports, extreme sports, and winter gear. Frasers said the partnership will allow Maxi Sport to maintain its top-tier retail format while unlocking future growth opportunities for Sports Direct stores in the region. “Maxi Sport represents the pinnacle of premium sports retail in Italy, and this partnership is the next phase of that journey,” said Frasers Group CEO Michael Murray. Mumbai-based fashion quick commerce startup ZILO has raised $15.3 million in a funding round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from existing investors InfoEdge Ventures and Chiratae Ventures, alongside Alteria Capital, Stride Ventures, and a group of angel investors. Founded by former Flipkart and Myntra executives Padmakumar Pal and Bhavik Jhaveri, ZILO promises 60-minute fashion delivery with features like home trials and instant returns. The platform currently partners with more than 200 fashion brands and is building a vertically integrated operating model focused on speed, assortment, and control. “This round validates our belief that fashion and speed don’t have to be trade-offs,” said co-founder and CEO Padmakumar Pal. “We’re building a new category where curated fashion meets the immediacy customers now expect.” Gordon Brothers has acquired the global LK Bennett brand and related IP assets from the Joint Administrators of LK Bennett Fashion Limited. The London-based heritage fashion label, founded by Linda Bennett in the 1990s, is celebrated for its refined British aesthetic, from limited-edition ready-to-wear to luxury shoes, bags, and accessories. “LK Bennett is a beloved heritage brand with a reputation for impeccable craftsmanship and quality,” said Tobias Nanda, Head of Brands at Gordon Brothers. “We are proud to steward the brand into its next phase of growth and bring its modern luxury to new global audiences.” Gordon Brothers plans to revitalize LK Bennett through an asset-light model, similar to its successful transformation of the Laura Ashley brand, by growing licensing, expanding e-commerce, and strengthening wholesale relationships. The firm will invest in new marketing strategies and product development to reinforce the brand’s position in the modern luxury space. LVMH has increased its ownership of Loro Piana to 94% through a €1 billion call option transaction, further deepening its ties with the Italian luxury brand. The move underscores LVMH’s confidence in Loro Piana’s long-term potential and strategic importance, now valuing the brand at €11 billion. Maria Luisa and Pier Luigi Loro Piana will remain on the board, ensuring the brand’s heritage is preserved. Loro Piana has become the third-largest fashion and leather goods business within LVMH, following Louis Vuitton and Dior, with estimated annual revenues of €2.5 billion. Frédéric Arnault, son of LVMH Chairman Bernard Arnault, was appointed CEO of Loro Piana in 2025, signaling the brand’s rising prominence. Since LVMH’s initial investment in 2013, the value of Loro Piana is believed to have quadrupled, driven by double-digit growth, increased investment in retail, and expanded product offerings in leather goods and homewares. China-based Anta Sports has acquired a 29.06% stake in Puma for €1.5 billion ($1.78 billion), becoming the German sportswear company’s largest shareholder. The deal, struck with Artémis, the Pinault family’s holding company, values Puma shares at €35 each and is expected to close by year-end, pending regulatory approval. The investment comes as Puma works to revive sales and momentum under CEO Arthur Hoeld, a former Adidas executive. Shares surged up to 20% on the news before settling around 9% higher. Anta said it has no current plans to acquire Puma outright. The move is part of Anta’s global expansion strategy and builds on its track record of acquiring Western sports brands, including the 2019 consortium-led acquisition of Amer Sports. Analysts say the deal could unlock synergies, with Puma’s strength in Europe and Latin America complementing Anta’s Asia-focused presence. Lands’ End and WHP Global have announced a strategic joint venture that will see WHP acquire a 50% controlling stake in the Lands’ End brand’s intellectual property for $300 million in cash. As part of the agreement, Lands’ End will contribute all brand-related IP and license agreements to the JV, while retaining full operational control of its DTC and B2B businesses. WHP Global will lead global licensing and brand expansion. The proceeds will be used to fully repay Lands’ End’s $234 million term loan and support broader corporate initiatives. The JV aims to unlock brand value through WHP’s global licensing platform. Watches of Switzerland Group has acquired an 88% stake in Deutsch & Deutsch, a family-owned luxury watch and jewelry retailer based in Texas, with an option to acquire the remaining shares. Financial terms were not disclosed. The acquisition adds four Rolex-authorized showrooms in El Paso, Laredo, McAllen, and Victoria to the London-based company’s U.S. footprint. These locations will continue to operate under the Deutsch & Deutsch name, preserving the retailer’s brand as it nears its 100-year anniversary. Watches of Switzerland said the acquisition strengthens its U.S. showroom network, now including 25 Rolex-anchored locations. Richemont has signed an agreement to sell Baume & Mercier to Italy’s Damiani Group, marking a major move in the luxury watch sector. The acquisition will expand Damiani’s hard luxury portfolio, which includes Damiani, Salvini, Bliss, Calderoni, and Murano glassmaker Venini, as well as watch and jewelry retailer Rocca. The 200-year-old Baume & Mercier will join a family-run group with a strong multi-brand distribution footprint and plans for select mono-brand boutiques. Richemont will provide operational support during a 12-month transition period. Closing is expected in summer 2026, pending customary conditions. Applied Real Intelligence (A.R.I.), a U.S.-based growth investment firm, has made a strategic investment in October’s Very Own (OVO), the lifestyle brand founded by Aubrey “Drake” Graham, Oliver El-Khatib, and Noah “40” Shebib. The deal supports OVO’s continued global expansion across e-commerce, retail, and partnerships. Founded in Toronto in 2008, OVO has grown from a music collective into a globally recognized lifestyle brand, with stores in North America and London. Under CEO Derek “Drex” Jancar, the company is scaling its operations while staying rooted in cultural credibility and creative leadership. “OVO isn’t a moment; it’s a long-term movement,” said Dr. Zack Ellison, Founder and Managing General Partner at A.R.I. “We’re proud to back a brand that blends authenticity, celebrity influence, and disciplined execution, hallmarks of the next generation of iconic consumer brands.” Nike has quietly sold RTFKT, its digital products subsidiary known for virtual sneakers and NFT collectibles, marking the end of a chapter that began with its acquisition in 2021. The sale follows Nike’s move to shutter RTFKT last year and aligns with CEO Elliott Hill’s renewed focus on core sports categories and wholesale partnerships. RTFKT (pronounced “Artifact”) was acquired under former CEO John Donahoe as part of Nike’s push into digital and direct-to-consumer channels. The buyer and deal terms were not disclosed. In a brief statement, Nike said the sale “launches a new chapter for the company and its community,” adding that it will continue investing in digital innovation, particularly through gaming partnerships and virtual wearables. Marubeni Corporation has acquired UK-based Jacobson Group, owner of heritage sneaker brand Gola, as part of its strategy to build a scalable lifestyle brand platform anchored by R.G. Barry Corporation (RGB). The acquisition marks RGB’s first roll-up deal since Marubeni acquired it in 2024. Jacobson’s portfolio, led by Gola, a British brand founded in 1905 with strong roots in sport and fashion, is distributed in over 30 countries. The deal will combine Jacobson’s brand equity with RGB’s U.S.-based sales infrastructure to drive global growth. Marubeni’s Consumer Platform U.S. is focused on building next-generation consumer businesses under the company’s GC2027 strategy. The group plans to continue expanding its brand portfolio through synergistic acquisitions that reflect evolving consumer preferences. Italian luxury apparel company Zanieri has completed its reverse merger with Everlert, Inc. (OTC: EVLI), gaining control of the public entity and integrating its operations under the Everlert corporate structure. The deal marks Everlert’s formal transition into a global luxury platform with Zanieri as its core operating business. Based in Umbria, Zanieri is a vertically integrated producer of premium cashmere, known for its end-to-end manufacturing, sustainability standards, and proprietary remote tailoring technology. The merger establishes Zanieri as the controlling shareholder, positioning the newly structured public company for global expansion and long-term growth. “This merger completes Everlert’s transition into a public company with a real operating business, meaningful scale, and international reach,” said Richard Hawkins, CEO of Everlert. “Zanieri is not simply a fashion brand, it’s an industrial luxury platform with deep manufacturing expertise and a clear strategy for disciplined global growth.” Golden Goose has announced a new investment partnership with global private equity firm HSG, which will acquire a majority stake in the next-gen luxury brand. Temasek will join as a minority investor, alongside existing backer Permira, which will retain a strategic minority position. The deal supports Golden Goose’s international growth while preserving its Italian craftsmanship roots. CEO Silvio Campara will continue to lead the company, with Marco Bizzarri (ex-Gucci CEO) becoming Non-Executive Chairman. The brand, known for blending luxury, lifestyle, and sportswear, has seen revenue grow from €266M in 2020 to €655M in 2024, driven by strong DTC momentum and global expansion. The transaction is expected to close in summer 2026. MadaLuxe Group has acquired a majority stake in IPPOLITA, the New York-based fine jewelry house known for its sculptural designs, artisanal craftsmanship, and global following. The deal adds to MadaLuxe’s expanding portfolio of luxury fashion and lifestyle brands across categories including apparel, accessories, home, and spirits. The acquisition aligns with MadaLuxe’s strategy to invest in heritage-driven brands with enduring cultural relevance. IPPOLITA founder Ippolita Rostagno will continue as Chief Creative Officer, leading design across the brand’s signature 18k gold and sterling silver collections. “Joining MadaLuxe opens an exciting new chapter that protects our heritage while embracing new growth,” said Rostagno. The brand, which debuted at Bergdorf Goodman, has become a defining name in accessible fine jewelry and is sold through top luxury retailers worldwide. Newly launched luxury group Hulcan, founded by MILE co-founders Joe Wilkinson and Mario Maher, has acquired iconic fashion retailer MATCHES and its in-house label RAEY. The deal marks a major move in redefining the future of luxury commerce, with the two brands set to relaunch in 2026 under Hulcan’s innovative, omnichannel model. The acquisition includes the full IP portfolio of MATCHES, positioning Hulcan to revive and evolve the storied retailer with a sharper focus on profitability, digital transformation, and cultural relevance. Backed by investors including Frasers Group, Francesco Ragazzi, PagsGroup, LVMH Luxury Ventures Advisors, and the Hermès Family, Hulcan aims to integrate commerce, culture, media, and fashion in a single ecosystem. “We’re committed to preserving MATCHES’ legacy while transforming it for a new era of luxury,” said Maher. “This acquisition is foundational to building a connected, modern group that serves both brands and the next generation of luxury consumers.” Global asset advisory firm Gordon Brothers has acquired a majority interest in the intellectual property of the Rachel Zoe brand, aiming to accelerate its growth through expanded licensing, new product categories, and broader distribution. The investment solidifies Rachel Zoe’s evolution from celebrity stylist to influential lifestyle entrepreneur with a multi-channel media and consumer brand. Best known for her Bravo show The Rachel Zoe Project and editorial platform The Zoe Report, Zoe has built a business spanning apparel, home, fragrance, eyewear, and children’s products. She continues to lead the brand as Founder, Chief Creative Officer, and board member. “Rachel is a global fashion authority with a brand that resonates across style, media, and lifestyle,” said Tobias Nanda, Head of Brands at Gordon Brothers. “We’re excited to grow her legacy through strategic licensing and innovation.” Republic Brands Group (RBG) has acquired heritage fashion labels Joie, Equipment, and Current/Elliott for $36 million, forming a new division dubbed The Lux Group. The move marks a strategic expansion for RBG as it builds a portfolio of culturally resonant, commercially proven brands. RBG plans to pivot the labels from a retail-heavy model to a focus on DTC and wholesale, while expanding into new categories such as handbags, footwear, and accessories through licensing. The group will install new leadership and appoint dedicated creative directors for each brand. “We believe in the value and recognizability of these brands,” said CEO Sami Souid. “Each has an established customer base and a clear point of view that fits our long-term vision.” Republic Brands Group (RBG) has acquired heritage fashion labels Joie, Equipment, and Current/Elliott for $36 million, forming a new division dubbed The Lux Group. Prada Chairman Patrizio Bertelli emphasized shared values of “creativity, craftsmanship, and heritage,” while CEO Andrea Guerra noted the acquisition adds a “different and complementary dimension” to the group’s portfolio. Skims, the shapewear and apparel brand co-founded by Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede, has raised $225 million in a new funding round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, with participation from BDT & MSD Partners. The raise values the brand at $5 billion as it accelerates plans for product expansion, international growth, and a deeper push into physical retail. Launched in 2019, Skims has become a favorite among younger consumers thanks to its inclusive sizing, minimalist aesthetic, and Kardashian’s massive social media reach. The company, which expects to surpass $1 billion in net sales in 2025 and currently operates 20 retail locations across the U.S. and Mexico, will use the capital to grow its core intimates and shapewear lines, expand into apparel and activewear, and lay the foundation to become a retail-first business “This milestone reflects continued confidence in our long-term vision,” said CEO Jens Grede. “With disciplined execution, we’re ready to unlock Skims’ next phase of growth.” LVMH’s watch division has acquired a minority stake in Swiss movement manufacturer La Joux-Perret, strengthening a growing partnership aimed at advancing production and innovation across its watch brands, including TAG Heuer, Hublot, and Zenith. The move comes as LVMH’s Watches & Jewelry division reported €7.41B in revenue for the first nine months of 2025, marking a 1% organic year-over-year increase. Global investment firm Carlyle has officially taken control of The Very Group, marking the end of the Barclay family’s more than 20-year ownership of the UK-based online retail giant. Abu Dhabi-based IMI, another major lender, remains a key stakeholder in the business. The Very Group, formerly Shop Direct and owner of Very.co.uk and Littlewoods, said the move provides a “strengthened capital base and enhanced financial flexibility” to support its long-term growth plans. Backers Carlyle and IMI, who have supported the group since 2021, will work with management to drive innovation and enhance the customer experience through tech and data investments. “This marks an important milestone as we enter a new phase of growth,” said CEO Robbie Feather. “Carlyle and IMI’s continued support gives us a stronger foundation to deliver on our strategy and build momentum.” Lingerie startup Peachaus has secured a £250,000 investment from retail veteran Angus Monro, the former CEO of Matalan, who also joins the company as acting Chairman. The funding marks a strategic milestone as Peachaus gears up for national expansion and future fundraising. Founded in 2022 by ex-Topshop Fashion Director Gillian Ridley Whittle, Peachaus is redefining lingerie retail through its values-led, direct-to-women model, bringing bra fittings to workplaces, co-working hubs, and festivals, rather than relying on traditional retail spaces. Monro joins a high-profile investor group that includes former Michael Kors CEO Cedric Wilmotte, ex-Wacoal CEO Tracey Lewis, and Sweaty Betty founder Tamara Hill-Norton, who are all backing Peachaus’ mission to build a sustainable, health-conscious brand poised to disrupt the global lingerie market. LuxExperience B.V., the digital luxury group behind Mytheresa, Net-a-Porter, and Mr Porter, has agreed to sell off-price fashion site The Outnet to The O Group LLC for $30 million. The deal includes all key assets, including brand rights, inventory, customer data, and U.S. distribution infrastructure, as well as the transfer of The Outnet’s U.S. and U.K. workforce. The Outnet, which specializes in discounted designer fashion from previous seasons, generated €260 million in net sales in FY25. While LuxExperience will retain a commercial relationship, continuing to supply merchandise and operational support, the sale marks a shift toward a leaner off-price strategy centered on Yoox. “The transaction will allow The Outnet to achieve its full potential under a renewed independent, stand-alone business model,” said Michael Kliger, CEO of LuxExperience. “It also enables us to accelerate transformation across our infrastructure and focus on driving growth at Yoox.” The deal is expected to close in Q1 2026, pending regulatory approvals. Homecourt, the luxury home care brand founded by Courteney Cox in 2022, has raised $8 million in Series A funding to scale its team, expand retail partnerships, and prepare for international growth. The round was led by Cult Capital with $5 million, alongside participation from existing investors and friends contributing the remaining $3 million. Known for its elevated home essentials, ranging from dish soap and surface sprays to candles and body care, Homecourt has reportedly reached $30 million in sales, with hand wash now leading in dollar volume. “Homecourt just means everything to me,” Cox said. “I needed partners who understood my obsession with detail and Cult Capital really got it.” With the investment, the brand plans to deepen its retail presence beyond Nordstrom and Bluemercury, grow its small but efficient team, and continue innovating around its best-selling CeCe fragrance line. International expansion is on the horizon, with London eyed as a potential launch point. “This brand works because I won’t settle for 99 percent,” Cox said. “It has to be perfect.” French e-commerce player Showroomprivé is divesting its 51% stake in fashion platform The Bradery, selling it back to founders Timothée Linyer and Edouard Caraco for €43.6 million. The move comes as part of a broader effort to streamline operations and strengthen the company’s financial position following a difficult fiscal year marked by a €39.7 million loss. Originally acquired in 2022 for €10.2 million, The Bradery has seen rapid growth, tripling its turnover from €21.7 million in 2021 to €62.9 million in 2024. Showroomprivé will receive an initial €17 million payment, with additional proceeds tied to performance-based milestones. The transaction is expected to close by year-end, pending regulatory approvals. Chalhoub Group has made a strategic minority investment in the menswear brand Willy Chavarria, joining existing investor FAE Fashion Ventures. The deal, reportedly under $5M, supports the label’s continued global expansion and infrastructure development. Chavarria, known for his culturally conscious, identity-driven collections, will benefit from Chalhoub’s deep operational expertise and regional retail presence across the Middle East. The investment follows a period of accelerated growth for the brand, which has tripled its wholesale footprint and launched collaborations with Adidas, Don Julio, and Tinder since FAE’s initial investment in 2024. The partnership marks Chalhoub’s continued evolution from distributor to brand builder, aligning with its broader strategy to back values-driven designers with long-term potential. Webster Capital has also joined the cap table alongside Chalhoub and FAE. “Together, we’re building a global powerhouse that connects with people where they are,” said Willy Chavarria. “Chalhoub and FAE bring the kind of integrity and cultural understanding that makes this partnership feel like family.” British retail giant Frasers Group has acquired a majority stake in The Webster, a high-end U.S. multi-brand luxury retailer known for its curated selection of over 100 designer labels, including Chanel, Dior, and Gucci. The Miami-based retailer has seen consistent growth, with a 10% increase in revenue and an expanded footprint of 13 boutiques across North America. Founder and CEO Laure Hériard Dubreuil will retain a minority stake and continue to lead operations. Calling the deal “the start of a new chapter,” Dubreuil praised the alignment between The Webster’s vision and Frasers Group’s ambition, especially around digital innovation and brand building. The acquisition supports Frasers Group’s elevation strategy, aimed at bolstering its luxury offering through its Flannels division, which already operates more than 80 stores in the UK and Ireland and maintains partnerships with brands like Moncler and Saint Laurent. Colorado-based outdoor brand Halfdays has raised $10 million in a Series A round led by Kellwood Company, with participation from Dick’s Sporting Goods Ventures, model Taylor Hill, and others. Known for redefining women’s skiwear with a stylish, functional edge, Halfdays was co-founded by Ariana Ferwerda, Karelle Golda, and Olympian Kiley McKinnon. The brand, which has gained traction over the past five years, is now shifting from survival mode to growth mode. “It’s the difference between surviving and scaling,” said Ferwerda, reflecting on the milestone moment. Fueled by strong seasonal performance and high sell-through rates, the funding will support expansion of Halfdays’ winter and ski lines, entry into year-round performance wear, accelerated wholesale partnerships with retailers like Revolve and Shopbop, and investments in brick-and-mortar retail. DK Company has acquired a majority stake in German fashion brand IVY OAK, expanding its presence in the premium fashion segment and strengthening its position in the German market. As part of the deal, IVY OAK’s headquarters will relocate to Copenhagen under DK Company’s structure, while the brand’s creative studio will remain in Berlin. “With IVY OAK, we see a perfect match between a strong, design-driven brand and DK Company’s expertise in international marketing and distribution,” said Jens Obel, CEO and co-owner of DK Company. “This acquisition supports our strategy of investing in the premium segment, while staying true to the creative and sustainable DNA of the brand.” German fashion label Closed has officially found new owners following insolvency proceedings. The Böck family, known for their role in Marc O’Polo, and fashion executive Dieter Holzer have acquired the company in a strategic move to revive the premium denim and lifestyle brand. Closed’s headquarters will remain in Hamburg, ensuring continuity for its operations and team. The acquisition secures the future of the brand, which has long been known for its high-quality craftsmanship and contemporary European aesthetic. Details of the restructuring plan or future strategy have not yet been disclosed, but the new owners are expected to focus on stabilizing operations, strengthening wholesale and retail presence, and rebuilding brand equity across core markets. Artistic Milliners has acquired a majority stake in Cone Denim from Elevate Textiles, forming a new multinational entity that will operate under the iconic Cone Denim name. The deal, set to close in Q1 2026, merges key assets from both companies while preserving Cone’s independent identity and leadership. The newly formed company will offer end-to-end denim solutions, with operations across Mexico, China, Pakistan, and the U.S., including Artistic Milliners’ SFI facility in Los Angeles and garment facility in Parras. “Combining Cone’s legacy with our global infrastructure creates a platform with unmatched scale, speed, and flexibility,” said Murtaza and Omer Ahmed of Artistic Milliners. VF Corporation has entered into a definitive agreement to sell iconic workwear brand Dickies® to Bluestar Alliance LLC for $600 million in cash. The deal marks a strategic portfolio move for VF and positions Dickies® for its next phase of growth under new ownership. Founded in 1922, Dickies® is a globally recognized brand known for blending utility and style, with a presence in 55 countries and deep cultural roots in both workwear and streetwear. “Dickies® has a rich legacy, and we’re excited to unlock its full potential,” said Bluestar Alliance CEO Joseph Gabbay. VF CEO Bracken Darrell added, “This transaction supports our strategy to strengthen our balance sheet and focus on core growth opportunities.” Kering and Mayhoola “ jointly announce that they have agreed to amend their shareholders’ agreement (initially concluded at the time of Kering’s acquisition of a 30% stake in Valentino in 2023) and more specifically the framework of the evolution of Valentino’s shareholding. According to this amendment, the current ownership structure of the House of Valentino will not change before 2028 at the earliest.” Premium sportswear brand Castore has acquired 100% of British heritage label Belstaff from INEOS, marking a major step in Castore’s expansion into the premium lifestyle category. As part of the deal, INEOS will also make a significant strategic investment at the Castore holding company level to support future global growth. Belstaff, known for its iconic waxed jackets and motorcycle-inspired fashion, will benefit from Castore’s direct-to-consumer expertise, global supply chain, and network of elite sports partnerships. “Belstaff is a truly iconic brand with unparalleled heritage,” said Castore CEO and Co-Founder Tom Beahon. “It’s a dream come true to lead it into its next chapter, and we’re equally thrilled to welcome INEOS as a strategic partner as we scale Castore globally.” Luxury skiwear and lifestyle brand Perfect Moment has secured $6.6 million in financing to support its next phase of growth. The funding includes a $5.1 million loan from chairman Max Gottschalk and a $1.5 million investment from X Cubed Capital Management, led by Andrew Redleaf. The capital will enable Perfect Moment to accelerate its expansion following recent strategic moves, including the opening of a new European distribution hub in the Netherlands and a corporate restructuring to boost operational efficiency and gross margins. “These financings demonstrate strong confidence in Perfect Moment’s strategy and brand potential,” said Gottschalk. “We’re now positioned to capitalize on growth opportunities through fiscal 2026 and beyond.” UK-based premium travel brand Antler has acquired US fashion-forward luggage label Paravel, forming the foundation of a new global strategy to build a ‘House of Travel Brands’ with projected sales surpassing £100 million by 2029. Paravel, which had previously filed for bankruptcy, will retain its brand identity under Antler’s leadership, with a full relaunch slated for 2026. The acquisition brings Antler, Nere (Australia), and Paravel under the ATR Group, each representing distinct market positioning and regional appeal. “This move strengthens our global reach and diversifies our portfolio across style, audience, and geography,” said Antler MD Kirsty Glenne. “With Antler, Nere, and Paravel under one roof, we’re well positioned to lead the next era of premium travel goods.” San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey has joined performance footwear and apparel brand while on earth™ as a co-founder and investor, marking a major milestone for the fast-growing company. Known for his longtime association with Nike, McCaffrey’s move signals a deep commitment to building a brand from the ground up. Launched in fall 2024, while on earth™ designs versatile, sustainably made footwear and apparel built for intentional movement between training and daily life. “For Christian to join us at this stage speaks volumes,” said founder Todd Meleney. “His involvement is already shaping our future, and we’re just getting started.” UK-based online fashion retailer Debenhams has secured a new three-year debt facility of up to £175 million, maturing in August 2028. The new funding replaces a prior £125 million credit line set to mature in October 2026 and follows a comprehensive market review led by CEO Dan Finley. The financing, led by TPG Angelo Gordon, carries an interest rate comprising the Bank of England base rate plus 7.3% and is designed to enhance the group’s financial flexibility as it executes a multi-year turnaround strategy. The company, which also owns Karen Millen, now operates an e-commerce platform offering around 15,000 brands. “We’ve put in place a new facility, 12 months early, with strong lenders that aligns with and supports our new strategy, supercharging Debenhams and turning around our youth fashion brands,” said Finley. Brand management firm Authentic has acquired a 51% stake in a newly formed entity that will own and license the majority of Guess’ global intellectual property. The remaining 49% will be retained by Guess cofounders Maurice and Paul Marciano, Nicolai Marciano, and CEO Carlos Alberini. The San Francisco-based direct-to-consumer retailer, known for $50 cashmere sweaters and viral traction on Instagram and TikTok, continues to thrive even as other DTC players struggle. Iconiq Capital led the round with participation from DST Global, Notable Capital, Basis Set Ventures, and 8VC. “This milestone will help us accelerate our growth and continue delivering exceptional quality at radically fair prices,” the company said in a statement, adding that “what started with a $50 cashmere sweater has grown into a movement across apparel, home, beauty, wellness, and beyond. And we’re just getting started.
